Jokers.effect:
{{hl|green|1 in 4}} chance for each played {{hl|orange|8}} to create a {{Tarot|}} card when scored
{{room}}
Jokers.syn:
Compared to other Tarot-generating jokers, 8 Ball is slow to begin with. You would need to draw and play all four 8s in your deck to simply match the expected value of a {{J|Cartomancer}}, and even then, it's not unlikely that you'll whiff every trigger and end up with no Tarots for your effort. However, if you're patient enough to play towards it, you'll find it's one of the most effective Tarot generators in the game. Unlike other Jokers of its kind, an 8 Ball at maximum efficiency can create multiple Tarots ''per hand'' without copy effects, outpacing even a {{J|Vagabond}}.

The deck-fixing properties that Tarot cards provide can make it easier to play more 8s and thus recursively create more Tarots. The enhancements can help with scoring as well, making up for the rank's relative lack of scoring Jokers. All of this is especially effective if the player is able to get a {{Seal|Red}} on one of their 8s and then repeatedly copy it.

===[[Decks]]===
*{{D|Abandoned}} and {{D|Mad World}} work best with 8 Ball, as the smaller deck size allows for 8s to be played easier.
*{{D|Magic}}'s extra consumable slot is very helpful to hold useful Tarot cards.
*{{D|Ghost}} and {{D|Zodiac}} can potentially benefit from 8 Ball thanks to Spectral and Tarot cards that allow more 8s to be created.
*{{D|Blue}} gives an extra hand, giving 8 Ball more chances to hit.

===[[Poker hands]]===
*{{ph|Pair}} or {{ph|Three of a Kind}} of 8s is good to start.
*{{ph|Five of a Kind}} or {{ph|Flush Five}} wo
Jokers.anti:
===Decks===
*{{d|Nebula}}'s fewer consumable slots makes it harder to hold and use Tarot cards from 8 Ball.
*{{D|Black}}, {{D|Blast Off}} and {{D|Golden Needle}} do not work well with 8 Ball due to their lower amount of hands, which reduces the chances for 8 Ball to generate Tarot cards.

===Jokers===
*Any Joker that limits the amount of 8s that can be played, such as {{J|Half Joker}}, will also reduce the chances for 8 Ball to generate Tarot cards.

===Card Modifiers===
* 8 Ball may prevent the player from maximizing value from {{Seal|Blue|name=Blue Seals}}, especially when the tarots generate during the last hand and fill up all consumable slots.

Jokers.effect:
{{Mult|+3}} for each [[Jokers|{{hl|orange|Joker}}]] card
{{Currently|{{mult|+0}}}}
Jokers.syn:
===[[Decks]]===
*{{D|Black}} works well with the Abstract Joker, as it provides +1 Joker slot.
*Similarly, {{D|Five-Card Draw}} works even better with the Abstract Joker, as it provides +2 Joker slots.

===[[Poker hands]]===
This Joker will increase the Mult of all types of hands by the same amount.

===[[Jokers]]===
* Near the beginning of the game, this Joker works best with {{J|Riff-Raff}}, which creates up to two Jokers per round.
* It gains additional Mult when using any type of Negative Joker.
* This Joker can have anti-synergy with a lone {{J|Joker Stencil}}, since Abstract requires full slots, and Stencil requires empty ones. However, if there are ''multiple'' Joker Stencils, these two jokers can actually work quite well with each other, giving a good multiplicative bonus, which is backed up by the +mult from Abstract.

===[[Vouchers]]===
* {{V|Antimatter}} gives an additional Joker slot, and with it, the potential for another {{Mult|+3}}.

===[[Tags]]===
* The {{Tag|Negative}} lets the player hold more Jokers irrespective of current Joker slots, especially if combined with one or more {{Tag|Double}}s.
Jokers.anti:
===[[Decks]]===
*{{D|Painted}} and {{D|Blast Off}} are difficult to use with the Abstract Joker, as they have one Joker slot less than usual.
*Similarly, {{D|Cruelty}} is even more difficult to use with the Abstract Joker, as it has two Joker slots less than usual.
===[[Jokers]]===
*{{J|Ceremonial Dagger}} or {{J|Madness}} should not be used with this Joker, as they both destroy Jokers.
===[[Blinds and Antes|Blinds]]===
*{{Blind|Verdant Leaf}} generally requires selling a Joker, meaning that Abstract Joker will lose {{mult|3}}.

Jokers.effect: {{xmult|3}} on {{hl|orange|final hand}} of round
Jokers.unlock: Play {{hl|orange|200}} hands
Jokers.syn:
===[[Decks]]===
*{{D|Black}} reduces the available Hands for the player by -1, making it less punishing for the player to use their final hand.
*Similarly, {{D|Blast Off}} reduces the available Hands for the player by -2, making it less punishing for the player to use their final hand.
*{{D|Golden Needle}} reduces the player's Hands to 1, meaning Acrobat is automatically activated.

===[[Poker hands]]===
This Joker does not directly synergize with any hand. Strategies that involve winning the round with one high-scoring hand like Four of a Kind or Straight Flush can take advantage of this Joker by playing throwaway hands until the Acrobat is activated. Used like this, the Acrobat is virtually a {{xmult|3}}  on the entire round score. Conversely, a strategy revolving around playing multiple easy to make hands does not benefit as much.

===[[Jokers]]===
Due to its condition of needing the final hand to be played, Acrobat does have some relevant synergies for other Jokers:
* {{J|Dusk}} retriggers all cards of the final hand, increasing scoring power depending on card Enhancements.
* In general, any Joker that adds additive Mult will work well alongside Acrobat.
** {{J|Mystic Summit}} will usually be active alongside Acrobat as long as the player remembers to expend all remaining discards before the final hand.
* Scaling Jokers that require hands to be played (e.g. {{J|Square Joker}} and {{J|Wee Joker}}) also work well, as hands can be used to scale them before preparing the winn
Jokers.anti:
===[[Decks]]===
*{{D|Green}}: As expending all hands is necessary to activate Acrobat, it leaves no additional hands leftover for bonus Money, possibly less if all discards were used as well.
===[[Jokers]]===
*Jokers that decrease in value when playing hands (e.g. {{J|Seltzer}} and {{J|Ice Cream}}) will likely be used up faster, as Acrobat requires the player to exhaust all hands to trigger.
===[[Blinds and Antes|Blinds]]===
*If {{Blind|Crimson Heart}} debuffs Acrobat on the final hand, it cannot give its {{Xmult|3}}.
Jokers.strats: Acrobat is a useful Joker to have when playing against {{Blind|The Needle}} [[Blinds and Antes|Blind]], since The Needle will reduce the available hands for the player to only 1, ensuring the {{Xmult|3}} from Acrobat will be applied. It is also useful against {{Blind|The Wall}} and the {{Blind|Violet Vessel}}, since the player will often go through all of their available hands while trying to overcome the larger score thresholds from those two Blinds, and the {{Xmult|3}} may be just enough of a boost to get the player over the finish line.

Jokers.effect: Played cards with {{suit|Spade}} suit give {{Chips|+50}} when scored

Although a potential source of chips for any hand due to its high output, Arrowhead is strongest with Flush hands. These are:

*{{ph|Straight Flush}}
*{{ph|Flush House}}
*{{ph|Flush Five}}

* {{J|Smeared Joker}} allows Arrowhead to benefit from Club cards, increasing the scope of its usage.
** Club-based Jokers like {{J|Gluttonous Joker}} and {{J|Onyx Agate}} may be useful in this context.
* {{J|Blackboard}} may be useful with Arrowhead once the playe
Jokers.anti:

* While {{J|Four Fingers}} can make Flushes easier to play, it enables the player to do so with less overall cards, therefore the scoring power of Arrowhead is weakened if the player opts for a 4-card Spade Flush.

Jokers.effect: Each {{hl|orange|King}} held in hand gives {{xmult|1.5}}
Jokers.syn:
===[[Decks]]===
*{{D|Painted}} has a larger hand size, making this Joker easier to use.

===[[Poker Hands]]===
If the player builds their deck to be mostly Kings, it is best to level up smaller hands such as {{ph|High Card}} or {{ph|Pair}} to keep as many Kings in hand as possible.

===[[Jokers]]===
* {{J|Mime}} doubles this card's multiplier per King (to {{xmult|2.25}} per King).
* {{j|Reserved Parking}} has a 50% chance of giving {{Money|1}} for each King (or other face card) held in hand.
* {{J|Midas Mask}} can add a buff to scored Kings, providing an additional benefit thereafter when Kings are held in hand.
* {{J|Steel Joker}} can potentially have synergy with Baron if you're able to make Steel Kings to provide even more {{xmult|}}.
* {{J|Shoot the Moon}} makes a great pair with Baron, as the {{mult|+13}} from the Queens will each be multiplied by {{xmult|1.5}}. However, for the Queens to trigger before the Kings, you must physically move the Queens to the left of your Kings. {{J|Raised Fist}} effectively does the same thing. Both of these Jokers' +Mult effects are retriggered by {{J|Mime}}, allowing for double the {{Hl|Red|+Mult}} before the Baron starts giving {{xMult|}}
* If the player's deck is mostly comprised of Kings, {{J|Juggler}} and/or {{J|Troubadour}} can increase the maximum number of cards held in hand and thus allow Baron to trigger more times.
* Tarot generating Jokers like {{J|Vagabond}} can help trim your deck using {{Tarot|The Hanged Man}} to draw Kings
Jokers.anti:

*{{D|Five-Card Draw}} does not work well with this Joker due to the decreased hand size and banning of hand size-increasing Jokers.

===Jokers===
*{{J|Merry Andy}} and {{J|Stuntman}} reduce hand size, which means the player holds fewer Kings.

===[[Blinds and Antes|Blinds]]===
*{{blind|The Plant}} is a run killer; debuffed Kings render Baron completely useless.
*{{Blind|The Psychic}} can be a run killer as well—scoring is reliant on playing 5 cards, therefore significantly reducing hand size.
*{{Blind|The Ox}} sets your money to zero if you play your most often played hand. This is especially detrimental in deep endless runs, where money is essential.
*{{Blind|The Mark}} draws all face cards face down, making it hard to tell which card is a King.

Jokers.strats:
On first glance, Baron might seem like a small amount of Mult. However, what makes Baron so incredibly strong is that every King or Steel card in hand multiplies your score exponentially. For example, one King only multiplies your score by 1.5x. But two Kings multiplies it by 1.5x twice, which is a 2.25x increase. If an ideal card for Baron is held in hand (a steel King with a red seal), it will produce x1.5⁴ = ~x5.1 Mult. With Mime, this increases to x1.5⁶ = ~x11.4 Mult; with one Blueprint/Brainstorm copying Mime, it increases to x1.5⁸ = ~x25.6 Mult, and with two cards copying each Mime and Baron it rises further to x1.5¹² = ~x130 Mult.

If a player manages to find these four Jokers and enough steel Kings with red seals to fill a hand, they will be able to play far into Endless mode. For example, with a Hand size of eight, the base Mult would be multiplied by ~x619 trillion; with a Hand size of nine this increases to ~80 quadrillion; and with a Hand size of ten it further increases to ~10 quintillion (1.0x10¹⁹). With some base chips and mult, this is enough to finish the first 16 Antes. Using this strategy, players can achieve the elusive [[Naneinf]] score, most often on {{D|Plasma}} due to its score balancing mechanic lowering the amount of cards necessary, or on {{D|Ghost}} due to easier access to Spectral cards such as {{Spectral|Deja Vu}} to apply a [[Red Seal]] and {{Spectral|Cryptid}} to copy cards, as well as temporarily bypass the hand size limit.

Brainstorm's disadvantage is that xMult Jokers (such as {{J|Cavendish}}) must be placed all the way to the left to be copied by Brainstorm, meaning the player cannot multiply the Mult from +Mult Jokers such as {{J|Supernova}} twice. For example, Supernova + Blueprint + The Trio will score more than The Trio + Supernova + Brainstorm. However, a {{edition|Polychrome}} Brainstorm can copy a +Mult Joker to its left while still allowing the full benefit of its edition effect. Some notable targets for copying include Jokers that make money mid-Blind such as {{J|Mail-In Rebate}}, retrigger Jokers such as {{J|Dusk}}, and xMult Jokers that trigger before most +Mult jokers anyways, such as {{J|Baron}}, {{J|Photograph}} or {{J|Bloodstone}}. When multiple copies are combined with Baron and Mime, usually while using {{D|Plasma}}, players can achieve the elusive [[Naneinf]] score.

When copying a Blueprint, Brainstorm will copy whichever effect Blueprint is copying, not the Blueprint itself.

While it will not work with them, Jokers such as {{J|Smeared Joker}} and {{J|Four Fingers}} can be used to unlock Brainstorm more easily.

Jokers.effect:
Create a {{Tarot|}} card when [[Blinds|{{hl|orange|Blind}}]] is selected
{{room}}

Moreover, acquiring {{Tarot|The Hermit}} or {{Tarot|Temperance}} early from this Joker's effect can help this Deck reach its ceiling sooner by overstepping its largest weakness: its poor early-game economy.
* {{d|Magic}}: This 52-stack of wizardry starts the player with the {{V|Crystal Ball}} Voucher, giving an extra consumable slot to hold more Tarot cards. This serves several functions when combined with this Joker: scoring-oriented Tarot cards like {{Tarot|Justice}} can be stored to save a run in a pinch; the starting copies of {{Tarot|The Fool}} will have easier access to more desirable targets, and potentially unwanted Tarot cards can be stored to prevent them from reappearing elsewhere. Obtaining earlier access to the {{V|Omen Globe}} Voucher can be of potential interest, too - by allowing [[Spectral cards]] to appear in {{Booster|Arcana}}s, they can be viewed as potential mini-Spectral Packs, as there would already be a reliable source of Tarot cards.

===[[Poker hands]]===
Cartomancer does not synergize directly with any poker hand. It provides very slight favor to the 5-card hands, however, as they provide more opportunities for Enhancements (applied by Tarot cards) to pump up the score.

===[[Jokers]]===
The following Jokers have synergy with Cartomancer:
* {{j|Fortune Teller}}: Perhaps the strongest synergy that either of these two have, it will
Jokers.anti:
===[[Decks]]===
*{{D|Nebula}}'s -1 consumable slot can make it harder to hold and use Tarot cards from Cartomancer.
* {{d|Anaglyph}}: With emphasis placed on skipping Blinds for duplication of powerful [[Tags]], it has slight anti-synergy with this Joker. It can still be very useful early on, however, especially in the absence of particularly strong Tags.
===[[Jokers]]===
* {{j|Throwback}}: A Joker that encourages skipping Blinds. Cartomancer will have fewer opportunities to create Tarot cards if scaling Throwback is more of a priority.

Jokers.effect:
This Joker gains {{Chips|+3}} per discarded [[Card Suits|{{hl|orange|[suit]}}]] card, suit changes every round
{{currently|{{chips|+0}}}}
Jokers.syn:
===[[Decks]]=== 
*The {{D|Checkered}} works well with Castle due to the lower suit diversity.
*The {{D|Red}} can use its +1 discard for more scaling.
*The {{D|Plasma}} gets more value from the chips than any other deck.
*The {{D|Painted}} increases the player's hand size by two, which allows players to see and discard more cards desired by Castle.
*The {{D|Erratic}} can start with a lot of cards of a certain suit, making it easier to fix the deck for Castle.

===[[Poker hands]]===
*Because Castle scales based on discarding cards, it means that weaker, easier hands like {{Ph|High Card}} and {{Ph|Pair}} allow for the effect to be used more consistently.
*Alternately, when players manage to shape their deck down to a single suit, Flush-based hands like {{Ph|Flush}}, {{Ph|Straight Flush}}, {{Ph|Flush House}}, and {{Ph|Flush Five}} become much more viable.

===[[Jokers]]===
*{{J|Drunkard}} and {{J|Merry Andy}} both provide additional discards, allowing Castle to scale more per round.
*{{J|Yorick}} will also scale alongside Castle.
*{{J|Smeared Joker}} makes Castle twice as easy to scale.
===[[Vouchers]]===
*{{V|Paint Brush}} and {{V|Palette}} increase the player's hand size, allowing players to see more of their deck and give them more chances to discard cards chosen by Castle.
*{{V|Wasteful}} and {{V|Recyclomancy}} both give 1 extra discard, allowing Castle to scale faster.

===[[Blinds and Antes|Blinds]]===
* {{Blind|The Hook}} automatically discards 2 cards held in hand, which
Jokers.anti:

*{{D|Green}} incentivizes not discarding, as it basically means throwing money away, which can make Castle difficult to use.
*{{D|Blast Off}} doesn't work well with Castle, as this deck only starts with 2 discards.
===[[Jokers]]===
*{{J|Burglar}} prevents this Joker entirely from scaling.
*{{J|Banner}}, {{J|Delayed Gratification}}, {{J|Green Joker}}, and {{J|Ramen}} conflict with this Joker, as their effects rely on not using discards.

===[[Blinds and Antes|Blinds]]===
* {{Blind|The Goad}}, {{Blind|The Head}}, {{Blind|The Club}}, and {{Blind|The Window}} all debuff a specific suit, preventing Castle from scaling if it happens to pick the to-be-debuffed suit upon entering the Boss Blind. One trick to avoid this is to check Castle

Jokers.effect:
{{xmult|3}}
{{hl|green|1 in 1000}} chance this card is destroyed at the end of round
Jokers.syn:
===[[Decks]]===
This Joker works well with any of the Decks, as it gives {{xmult|3}} to every hand played.
===[[Poker hands]]===
Any hand can benefit from this Joker for the same reasons that any of the Decks can.
===[[Jokers]]===
* Cavendish, as any Multplicative Mult Joker, pairs incredibly well with Additive Mult Jokers and other Multiplicative Mult Jokers, especially scaling ones. This includes Jokers such as {{J|Green Joker}}, {{J|Fortune Teller}} and {{J|Flash Card}}.
* Copying Cavendish with {{J|Blueprint}} and {{J|Brainstorm}} does not increase the probability of self-destruction of Cavendish or cause the copying Joker to self-destruct, so they can be used without additional risks.
Jokers.anti:
* {{J|Oops! All 6s}} doubles Cavendish's destruction chance to a {{Hl|green|2 in 1000}} chance. This can safely be ignored in most cases.
** To guarantee that Cavendish gets destroyed, the player would need 10 copies of {{J|Oops! All 6s}} (which would display as a {{Hl|green|1024 in 1000}} chance).
Jokers.strats:
* The {{D|Non-Perishable}} challenge bans Cavendish.
* While Cavendish can also go "Extinct!", it is still able to show up in the shop again, unlike {{J|Gros Michel}}.

Jokers.effect:
When [[Blinds|{{hl|orange|Blind}}]] is selected, destroy [[Jokers|Joker]] to the right and permanently add {{hl|orange|double}} its sell value to this {{hl|red|Mult}}
{{currently|{{mult|+0}}}}
Jokers.syn:
===[[Decks]]===
*{{D|Yellow}} is a good option, as the early bonus money allows players to get to {{Money|25}} quickly and be able to save up a lot for the Dagger.
*{{D|Black}}'s extra Joker slot is very helpful, as one can still have four safe Jokers while scaling Dagger.
*Similarly,{{D|Five-Card Draw}}'s 2 extra Jokers slots is even better, as one can still have six Jokers while scaling Dagger.
*{{D|Anaglyph}} is occasionally a good choice, as the Double Tag can provide lots of economic buffs when presented. However, skipping a blind means skipping a level of scaling.
*{{D|Inflation}} might work with Ceremonial Dagger, as this deck permanently increases prices by {{$|1}} on every purchase, including the sell price. This Joker can scale very fast thanks to Jokers' inflated sell prices.

===[[Poker hands]]===
This Joker can sometimes make it more difficult to change your deck due to needing a constant supply of money to fuel its destruction of other Jokers. As a result, it might be best to prioritize easier-to-play hands. However, the hand you play doesn't really matter, as the Mult Dagger provides will always apply.

===[[Jokers]]===
Ceremonial Dagger is, at its core, an economy-based scaling Joker. Therefore, having more money makes it better, as one can afford more expensive Jokers to scale it. There are many options, but it's recommended to go for more powerful ones, like {{J|Cloud 9}} or {{J|Golden Ticket}}, as Joker slots are limited with Dagger.

* Jokers that expire g
Jokers.anti:
===[[Decks]]===
*{{D|Painted}}'s reduced Joker amount is bad to combo with Ceremonial Dagger, as the player will only have three Jokers while scaling Ceremonial Dagger.
*Similarly, {{D|Cruelty}}'s reduced Joker amount is even more difficult to combo with Ceremonial Dagger, as the player will only have two Jokers while scaling Ceremonial Dagger.
*{{D|Non-Perishable}} does not work with Ceremonial Dagger, as all Jokers are {{Sticker|Eternal}}, and it cannot destroy them and doesn't gain {{Hl|Red|{{Mult|+}}}}.
===[[Jokers]]===
* {{J|Abstract Joker}} depends on having many Jokers to boost its {{hl|red|+Mult}}, which it can't do very well with Ceremonial Dagger destroying Jokers left and to the right, which reduces the total Joker count.
* {{J|Throwback}} depends on skipping Blinds, and when a Blind is skipped, Ceremonial Dagger cannot be upgraded.

===[[Vouchers]]===
* {{v|Clearance Sale}} a
Jokers.strats: Ceremonial Dagger has high growth potential, while this requires an additional Joker Slot (used to place the Joker to be destroyed) to achieve. However, outside of the  {{D|On a Knife's Edge}} Challenge, Ceremonial Dagger ''can'' be used alongside other Jokers once it's buffed up significantly. Simply move it to the rightmost slot at the end of each blind, start a new blind, and move it back to the leftmost side so it can provide maximum effect for other Multiplicative Jokers. This ensures Ceremonial Dagger doesn't consume any other Jokers while still providing {{hl|red|+Mult}} for the round. On {{Stake|Black}} difficulty or higher (and in some Challenges), it is also possible to put an {{Sticker|Eternal}} Joker to the right of it and prevent Ceremonial Dagger from destroying Jokers.

Jokers.effect: When round begins, add a random {{hl|orange|playing card}} with a random [[Seal|{{hl|orange|seal}}]] to your hand
Jokers.unlock: Have a [[Gold cards|Gold playing card]] with a [[Gold Seal|{{hl|orange|Gold Seal}}]]
Jokers.syn:
===[[Decks]]===
* Because {{D|Magic}} starts with {{V|Crystal Ball}}, it allows the player to make better use of {{Seal|Blue}}s and {{Seal|Purple}}s.
* {{D|Painted}}'s extra hand size allows the player to hold more cards created by Certificate, as well as finding a desired hand whilst holding onto those cards more easily.
* {{D|Zodiac}} can use its extra Tarot cards to more easily manipulate the Sealed cards from Certificate.
* {{D|Abandoned}}'s and {{D|Mad World}}'s reduced deck size make it easier to find the produced cards after they have been added to the deck. It is also easier to flood these decks with high-quality cards, since there are fewer bad cards to potentially draw.

===[[Poker hands]]===
*No specific poker hand directly benefits from Certificate, but any of them can be leveled up with its generated {{Seal|Blue}}s. Hands that benefit more from planet cards therefore indirectly benefit more.
*If Certificate is held for only a couple of rounds, the generated cards are generally high-value duplication targets, and it can be easier to make powerful {{Ph|Five of a Kinds}} or {{Ph|Flush Fives}}.
*If Certificate is held for a long time or is {{Sticker|Eternal|image=Certificate.png}}, then lower value poker hands like {{ph|High Card}} and {{ph|Pair}} that do not rely on finding specific cards can be easier to find with many extra random cards in the deck.

===[[Jokers]]===
* {{J|Hologram}} scales with each card Certificate adds.
* {{J|DNA}} is better when copying valuab
Jokers.anti:
===[[Decks]]===
* {{D|Nebula}} makes it significantly harder to use Blue and Purple Seals due to the starting 1 consumable slot.
* On {{D|Checkered}} Certificate can still create {{Suit|Club}} and {{Suit|Diamond}} cards, which can make it harder to play flushes.

===[[Poker hands]]===
*If Certificate is held for a long time or is {{Sticker|Eternal|image=Certificate.png}}, then higher value poker hands like {{ph|Straight}} and {{ph|Four of a Kind}} that rely on finding specific cards can be much harder to find with many extra random cards in the deck.

===[[Jokers]]===
*{{J|Erosion}} relies on a small deck size, which is more difficult to get when 1 card is added per round from Certificate.

=== [[Blue Seal]] === 
{{main|Blue Seal#Anti-Synergies}}
* Cards that decrease the players hand size, like {{J|Stuntman}} and {{Spectral|Ouija}} can make finding and holding Blue seals more difficult.
Jokers.strats:
* When Certificate adds a sealed card at the beginning of the round, it is put directly into your hand, bypassing the normal hand size temporarily.
* Certificate does not prevent the player from dying when they have a hand size of zero or below, since the game checks the hand size before Certificate can activate.
*Unlike other Jokers that activated "When a blind is selected", Certificate activates "when a round begins", which is when the initial hand is drawn. This means Blueprint / Brainstorm can be used to copy for example {{J|Cartomancer}}, then immediately moved over to copy Certificate after clicking Select Blind (best done at lower game speeds).
* The {{D|Fragile}} challenge bans Certificate.

Jokers.effect: {{hl|orange|1}} free {{hl|green|Reroll}} per shop
Jokers.syn:
===[[Decks]]===
* {{D|Zodiac}} works well with this Joker, as you will want to be rerolling more to see more Tarot and Planet cards.
* {{D|Black}} is decent for this Joker, as rerolling a lot allows you to see more Jokers that you can take.
===[[Jokers]]===
* {{J|Flash Card}}: use the free reroll to boost this after every shop visit.
* {{J|Campfire}}: can scale quicker, as the free reroll can let you find more [[Jokers]] or [[Consumables]] to buy and sell.
* {{J|Constellation}}: can scale very quickly, as the free reroll can let you find more planet cards each shop.
* {{J|Astronomer}}: can let you find more free planet cards.
=== [[Vouchers]] ===
* {{V|Overstock}} and {{V|Overstock Plus}} can make Chaos's free reroll much more significant.
* {{V|Reroll Surplus}} and {{V|Reroll Glut}} combined with Chaos is practically equivalent to a {{tag|D6}}.

*On {{Stake|Gold}}, Chaos the Clown can be {{Sticker|Rental}}, allowing the player to purchase it for {{Money|1}}, get a free re-roll, and then sell it back again for {{Money|1}} to remain money neutral.

* Multiple copies of Chaos the Clown (obtained through {{spectral|Ankh}}, {{j|Invisible Joker}}, or {{j|Showman}}) do stack, allowing the player to get 2 free rerolls. However, it cannot be copied {{J|Blueprint}} or {{J|Brainstorm}}.

Jokers.effect: Disables effect of every [[Blinds|{{hl|orange|Boss Blind}}]]
Jokers.unlock: Find this [[Jokers|Joker]] from the [[the Soul|{{hl|sblue|Soul}}]] card.
Jokers.syn:
===[[Decks]]===
*{{d|Black}} has +1 Joker slot, which leaves more room for scoring Jokers.

=== [[Jokers]] ===
Boss Blinds can affect almost every Joker in the game, and thus be helped by Chicot, but many Jokers have notable weaknesses to particular Boss Blinds. Chicot can negate the holes in these Jokers' defenses:
* {{J|Photograph}}, {{J|Smiley Face}}, and other [[face card]] Jokers no longer fear {{blind|The Plant}} or {{Blind|The Mark}}.
** In this context, {{J|Pareidolia}} becomes less punishing to use.
* {{J|Bloodstone}}, {{J|Seeing Double}}, and other [[Card Suits|Card Suit]] Jokers can ignore their respective Boss Blinds.
** In particular, {{J|Flower Pot}} and {{J|Ancient Joker}} can safely rely on Wild cards with Chicot.
* {{J|Card Sharp}}, {{J|Supernova}}, and other Jokers limited by [[poker hand]]-limiting Boss Blinds.
* {{J|Burglar}} is no longer weak against {{Blind|The Mouth}} or {{Blind|The Fish}}.
* Any {{J|Oops! All 6s}} based run will no longer fear {{Blind|The Wheel}}.
* Jokers that rely on discards (by either keeping them or using them), such as {{J|Banner}} or {{J|Castle}}, can safely ignore {{Blind|The Water}}.

===[[Boss Blinds]]===
Disabling a boss blind reverses its effect, and due to the timing involved, multiple copies of {{J|Chicot}} will all disable the Boss Blind, resulting in a net positive effect:
* {{Blind|The Wall}}: Score requirement is reduced by a factor of 2 for each copy of Chicot.
* {{Blind|The Water}}: Gains the number of discards orig
Jokers.anti:
===Decks===
*{{d|Painted}}, {{D|Blast Off}} and {{D|Cruelty}} penalize holding non-scoring Jokers like Chicot with their reduced Joker slots.
===Jokers===
* As {{J|Luchador}} also disable Boss blinds, functionally overlapping with Chicot, Luchador becomes a redundant pickup.
* {{J|Matador}} also does not work, as it activates based on Boss Blind effects.
===Vouchers===
* The {{V|Director's Cut}} and {{V|Retcon}} vouchers are usually made obsolete with the possession of Chicot, since Boss Blind effects are no longer a concern.
===Blinds===
* While normally it's not too big of a problem, do note that {{Blind|Amber Acorn}} shuffles Jokers before Chicot disables it, which can be annoying sometimes.
* Any run that relies on {{Blind|The Serpent}}'s effect will no longer work with Chicot.

Jokers.effect: {{Chips|+80}} if played hand contains a {{ph|Two Pair}}
Jokers.syn:
===[[Decks]]===
*{{d|Abandoned}} and {{D|Mad World}} work well with this Joker thanks to their smaller deck, allowing you to find a Two Pair easier.
*{{d|Erratic}} can work well with this Joker if it randomizes a lot of cards with the same rank.
*{{d|Plasma}} benefits from the large amount of chips, which, when balanced, greatly boost the score for the played hand.
===[[Poker hands]]===
Any Poker Hand that contains a Two Pair will benefit from Clever Joker. These are:
*{{ph|Two Pair}}
*{{ph|Full House}}
*{{ph|Flush House}}
*{{ph|Flush}} - only if the flush contains a Two Pair

{{Ph|Four of a Kind}} and similar hands do '''not''' trigger Clever Joker.
===[[Jokers]]===
*{{j|Spare Trousers}} gains Mult when playing a Two Pair.
*{{j|Square Joker}} gains Chips any time a played hand consists of exactly 4 cards. Since a standard Two Pair is exactly four cards, the player can strengthen Square Joker while getting Chips from Clever Joker.
*{{j|Jolly Joker}} and {{j|Mad Joker}} give Mult on a Pair and Two Pair respectively.
*{{j|Sly Joker}} gives Chips if the played hand contains a Pair.
*{{j|The Duo}} provides a {{Xmult|2}} boost when playing a Two Pair.

Jokers.effect:
Earn {{Money|1}} for each {{hl|orange|9}} in your {{hl|orange|full deck}} at end of round
{{Currently|{{Money|4}}}}
Jokers.syn:
===[[Decks]]===
Any Deck can use Cloud 9 effectively, as it pays out whenever a round is completed as long as the player has at least one 9 in their full Deck.

* {{D|Black}} can benefit from Cloud 9 thanks to its +1 Joker Slot. Because of the -1 hand per blind penalty, Cloud 9 can help offset the lower income from early games.
* {{d|Green}}: This Deck likes to have extra income sources in the absence of interest, so something like Cloud 9 is a natural inclusion.
* {{d|Yellow}}: This Joker will help maintain the interest cap when acquired in the mid-game, further increasing the already-strong buying power it has.
* {{d|Ghost}}, {{d|Magic}}, and {{d|Zodiac}}: All these Decks have easier access to Deck fixing to include a higher amount of 9s in the Deck. Of these, Ghost Deck is probably the best to choose, as its starting {{Spectral|Hex}} [[Spectral card]] makes it more practical to keep this Joker for the long run by allowing it to help with scoring.
===[[Poker hands]]===
Since players are encouraged to create lots of 9s to increase Cloud 9's benefit, hands which use many of the same rank are recommended.
* {{ph|Three of a Kind}}
* {{ph|Four of a Kind}}
* {{ph|Five of a Kind}}
* {{ph|Flush Five}}
===[[Jokers]]===
* [[Tarot card]] generation is extremely important if the maximization of Cloud 9's value is the goal. {{j|Cartomancer}} is the most effective one, creating a Tarot card whenever a Blind is selected (a Cloud 9 build would not want to skip in the first place in order t
Jokers.anti:
===Decks===
*{{D|Painted}}, {{D|Blast Off}} and {{D|Cruelty}}: The reduced Joker slots makes it difficult to carry Cloud 9 since players may need more scoring Jokers to survive and beat Ante 8.

Jokers.effect:
This Joker gains {{xmult|0.1}} every time a [[Planet_Cards|{{hl|cyan|Planet}}]] card is used
{{currently|{{xmult|1}}}}
Jokers.syn:
=== [[Decks]] ===
* {{D|Nebula}} begins with the {{V|Telescope}} Voucher, allowing the player to purchase a [[Planet card]] of the most played Poker Hand each time a {{Booster|Celestial}} is opened.
* {{D|Zodiac}} begins with the {{V|Planet Merchant}} Voucher making Planet cards have a x2 chance of appearing.

=== [[Poker Hands]] ===
Since Constellation levels up regardless of the [[Planet cards]]' type, any poker Hand has synergy with it.

=== [[Jokers]] ===
* Economy Jokers (ex. {{J|Business Card}}, {{J|Golden Joker}}, {{J|Cloud 9}}, etc.) are important to help scale Constellation, since they allow the player to purchase more {{Booster|Celestial}}s and [[Planet cards]] from the [[The Shop|Shop]].
** Notably, {{J|Satellite}} provides more money for each unique Planet card used.
* {{J|Chaos the Clown}} gives a free reroll in the Shop allowing for more Planet cards to be found.
* {{J|Mime}} is able to retrigger a {{Seal|Blue}}, allowing for two Planet cards to be created, instead of one.
* {{J|Astronomer}} makes every Planet card and {{Booster|Celestial}} in the Shop free, thus giving free upgrades to Constellation.
* {{J|Certificate}} can generate cards with a {{Seal|Blue}}, granting a repeatable source of Planet cards.
* As {{J|Perkeo}} gives a copy of a random consumable at the end of the Shop, the player should keep a Planet card of their best poker hand to obtain more, and scale Constellation.

===[[Vouchers]]===
*{{v|Overstock}} and {{v|Overstock Plus}} respectively add
Jokers.anti:

*{{J|Red Card}} encourages skipping {{Booster|Celestial}}s instead of using the Planet cards in them.
*{{J|Campfire}} incentives the player to sell Planet cards instead of using them.
*Skipping for {{J|Throwback}} or {{J|Diet Cola}} likely means fewer Planet cards to find or use, although this becomes viable if the {{Tag|Meteor}} is involved.

*{{V|Tarot Merchant}}, {{V|Tarot Tycoon}}, and {{V|Magic Trick}} reduce the probabilities of Planet cards appearing in the shop.

Jokers.effect: {{Chips|+80}} if played hand contains a {{ph|Flush}}
Jokers.syn:
===[[Decks]]===
*{{d|Checkered}} works best with Crafty Joker thanks to its 2 suits, allowing Flushes to be reliably formed.
*{{d|Plasma}} benefits from the large amount of chips, which, when balanced, greatly boost the score for the played hand.
===[[Poker hands]]===
Playing any kind of Flush will trigger Crafty Joker. This includes:
*{{ph|Flush}}
*{{ph|Straight Flush}}
*{{ph|Flush House}}
*{{ph|Flush Five}}
===[[Jokers]]===
*{{j|Smeared Joker}} and {{J|Four Fingers}} make it easier to play Flushes.
*{{j|Droll Joker}} gives {{Mult|+10}} when playing a Flush.

Jokers.effect: {{Mult|+12}} if played hand contains a {{ph|Straight}}
Jokers.syn:
===[[Decks]]===
* {{D|Red}} is good with this joker, as more discards can help you get a Straight.
* {{D|Nebula}} can be good, as having your hands be mainly Straight means having your planet packs contain {{Planet|Saturn}} helps.
* {{D|Abandoned}} and {{D|Mad World}} both have fewer cards than a standard deck, which makes Straights easier to make.
* {{D|Painted}} gives extra hand size, which can help the player with forming Straights.
*{{D|15 Minute City}} starts with an Eternal {{Sticker|Eternal|image=Shortcut.png|link=Shortcut|name=Shortcut}}, which allows Straights to be made with gaps in them, making it easier to get that hand.

Crazy Joker affects both {{Ph|Straights}} and {{ph|Straight Flushes}}.

* {{J|Devious Joker}}, {{J|Runner}}, and {{J|The Order}} will always activate at the same time as this Joker, as well as possibly {{J|Superposition}} and {{J|Séance}}, though those are more specific.

*{{V|Wasteful}} and {{v|Recyclomancy}} give additional discards, allowing the player to search for Straight hands easier.

*{{V|Telescope}} can help upgrade Straights using {{planet|Saturn}}.

===Decks===
* {{D|Erratic}} has anti-synergy, as it is generally harder to create Straights with this deck.
*{{D|Five-Card Draw}}'s -3 hand size makes it extremely hard to assemble Straights.

===[[Jokers]]===
*Jokers that reduce hand size, like {{j|Stuntman}} and {{j|Merry Andy}}, have anti-synergy with Crazy Joker, as a smaller hand size makes it harder to assemble Straights.

*{{Spectral|Ectoplasm}} and {{Spectral|Ouija}} have anti-synergy with Crazy Joker, as a smaller hand size makes it harder to assemble Straights. Not only that, but {{Spectral|Ouija}} converts all cards held in hand into one single rank, which makes assembling Straights less consistent.

*{{Blind|The Manacle}}'s -1 hand size makes it hard to assemble Straights.
*{{Blind|The Water}} will always start with 0 discards, making it very hard to assemble Straights.

Jokers.effect: Go up to {{hl|red|-$20}} in debt
Jokers.syn:
===[[Decks]]===
*{{D|Green}} does not generate interest based on current money, which means being in debt does not hinder your income.
*{{D|Luxury Tax}}: When playing this challenge deck, hand size decreases by 1 for every {{Money|5}}, meaning that with a single credit card, the hand size can be increased by up to 4. Additionally, having a credit card makes it easier to avoid the hand size penalty while still being able to buy items from the shop.

===[[Jokers]]===
*{{J|Vagabond}} allows you to get Tarot cards every time you play a hand with {{Money|4}} or less. Staying in debt with the Credit Card assures you will create many Tarot cards.
*{{J|Credit Card}}: Although the wording may make it seem otherwise, multiple copies '''do''' stack, allowing you to go up to {{Money|40}} in debt with two, up to {{Money|60}} with three, etc., if that's something you would want.
**Credit Card cannot be copied by {{J|Blueprint}} or {{J|Brainstorm}}, but multiple copies can be obtained via {{J|Showman}}, {{J|Invisible Joker}}, or {{Spectral|Ankh}}.

===[[Blinds and Antes|Blinds]]===
*{{Blind|The Ox}}: Playing your most played hand this run sets money to {{Money|0}}, which can be used to wipe out Credit Card's debt.
*{{Blind|The Tooth}}: Losing money is less detrimental with the ability to go into debt, but be careful, as you may lose a lot of money and go deeply below -{{Money|20}}.

===[[Consumables]]===
*{{Spectral|Wraith}} sets your money to {{Money|0}} after use, meaning you gain money i
Jokers.anti:
=== Decks ===
* {{D|Rich get Richer}}: Since chips cannot exceed the current money, being in debt will prevent the player from scoring any points at all.
	
=== Jokers ===
* {{J|To the Moon}}: Without any money, no interest can be generated.
* {{J|Bull}} does not have any effect if you don't have any money.
* {{J|Bootstraps}} also has no effect for the same reason.
	
=== Vouchers ===
* {{V|Seed Money}} and {{V|Money Tree}}: No interest can be earned if the player is in debt.
	
===Consumables===
*{{Tarot|The Hermit}} Tarot card (which normally doubles your money) gives no money if you have {{Money|0}} or less.
Jokers.strats: * The {{D|Inflation}} and {{D|Golden Needle}} [[Challenge Decks|challenges]] start the player with a copy of Credit Card.

Jokers.effect: Earn {{Money|2}} per {{hl|orange|discard}} if no discards are used by end of the round
Jokers.syn:
===[[Decks]]===
*{{D|Red}} provides an additional discard, which increases the money earned when this Joker is triggered.
*{{D|Painted}} has a larger hand size, which increases the likelihood of drawing a strong [[Poker Hand]] without discarding.
*{{D|Green}} already incentivizes using few discards.
*{{D|Five-Card Draw}} and {{D|Golden Needle}} both start with 6 discards, which means Delayed Gratification can provide {{Money|12}} if no discards are used. However, {{D|Golden Needle}} starts with only 1 hand, which can make it awkward to use Delayed Gratification.

===[[Poker hands]]===
This Joker disincentivizes discarding, so it is recommended to play more common poker hands like {{Ph|High Card}}, {{Ph|Pair}}, {{Ph|Two Pair}}, or {{Ph|Three of a Kind}}.

===[[Jokers]]===
*Works well with any Jokers that reward you for not discarding, especially {{J|Banner}}, {{J|Green Joker}}, and {{J|Ramen}}.
*Any Joker that increases the number of discards (for example, {{J|Drunkard}} or {{J|Merry Andy}}) will benefit Delayed Gratification.
**Though Merry Andy decreases hand size, which could make it harder to form hands.
*Jokers that make poker hands easier to make, like {{J|Shortcut}}, {{J|Four Fingers}}, or {{J|Smeared Joker}}, give the player an opportunity to win the round without using discards.
*Jokers that affect hand size, like {{J|Juggler}}, {{J|Turtle Bean}}, and {{J|Troubadour}}, make it significantly easier to form hands without discarding.
**However, {{J|Troubadour}} has a -1
Jokers.anti:
===[[Decks]]===
*{{D|Black}} makes it difficult to use Delayed Gratification due to its -1 hand per round.
*{{D|Blast Off}} is even worse due to its -2 hands and -1 discard per round.

===[[Poker hands]]===
Without heavy deck modification, strong five-card hands like {{Ph|Flush}}, {{Ph|Straight}}, or {{Ph|Full House}} will be hard to assemble without using any discards.

===[[Jokers]]===
*{{J|Burglar}} removes all discards, rendering Delayed Gratification useless.
*Jokers that encourage discarding, like {{J|Castle}}, {{J|Mail-In Rebate}}, {{J|Faceless Joker}}, {{J|Burnt Joker}}, and {{J|Yorick}}, all have anti-synergy with Delayed Gratification.
*{{J|Mystic Summit}} is especially bad, as it requires having no discards remaining.
*Jokers that decrease hand size, like {{J|Merry Andy}} and {{J|Stuntman}}, could make it much harder to form hands, as Delayed Gratification heavily encourages n
Jokers.strats: * {{Blind|The Hook}}'s forced discards will not prevent Delayed Gratification from taking effect.

Jokers.effect: {{Chips|+100}} if played hand contains a {{ph|Straight}}
Jokers.syn:
===[[Decks]]===
*{{D|Abandoned}} and {{D|Mad World}} both work best with Devious Joker thanks to their smaller card count, allowing Straights to be formed easier.
*{{D|Painted}} also works well with Devious Joker thanks to its larger hand size, allowing Straights to be formed easier.
*{{d|Plasma}} benefits from the large amount of chips, which, when balanced, greatly boost the score for the played hand.
*{{D|15 Minute City}} starts with an Eternal {{Sticker|Eternal|image=Shortcut.png|link=Shortcut|name=Shortcut}}, which allows Straights to be made with gaps in them, making it easier to get that hand.

===[[Poker hands]]===
Playing any {{Ph|Straight}} will trigger Devious Joker, including {{Ph|Straight Flush}} and {{Ph|Royal Flush}}.
===[[Jokers]]===
*{{j|Shortcut}} allows gaps in Straights, making them easier to find and play.
*{{j|Four Fingers}} allows Straights of length 4, making them easier to find and play.
*{{j|Runner}} gains Chips when playing a Straight.
*{{j|Crazy Joker}} gives {{Mult|+12}} when playing a Straight.
*{{j|The Order}} gives {{xMult|3}} when playing a Straight.

===[[Vouchers]]===
*{{V|Wasteful}} and {{v|Recyclomancy}} give additional discards, allowing the player to search for Straight hands easier.
*{{v|Paint Brush}} and {{v|Palette}} both increase hand size, which can help players with forming Straights.
Jokers.anti:
===[[Decks]]===
*{{d|Erratic}}'s randomness can make it harder to assemble Straights.
*{{D|Five-Card Draw}}'s -3 hand size makes it extremely hard to assemble Straights.

===[[Jokers]]===
*Jokers that reduce hand size, like {{j|Stuntman}} and {{j|Merry Andy}}, have anti-synergy with Devious Joker, as a smaller hand size makes it harder to assemble Straights.

===[[Consumables]]===
*{{Spectral|Ectoplasm}} and {{Spectral|Ouija}} have anti-synergy with Devious Joker, as a smaller hand size makes it harder to assemble Straights. Not only that, but {{Spectral|Ouija}} converts all cards held in hand into one single rank, which makes assembling Straights very difficult.

===[[Blinds and Antes|Blinds]]===
*{{Blind|The Manacle}}'s -1 hand size makes it harder to assemble Straights.
*{{Blind|The Water}} will always start with 0 discards, making it very hard to assemble Straights.

Jokers.effect: Sell this card to create a free [[Tags|{{hl|orange|Double Tag}}]]
Jokers.syn:
===[[Decks]]===
*{{D|Black}}: The +1 Joker slot gives more chances to get Diet Cola without having to sell another Joker.
*{{D|Anaglyph}}: Diet Cola's Double Tag can stack with the ones obtained after defeating a boss blind.

===[[Jokers]]===
Diet Cola synergizes with just about every build as long as the player has an open Joker slot. It is, in effect, a {{Money|3}} Double Tag, if it is bought and sold immediately. Any build that is empowered by a tag is inherently empowered by buying and selling Diet Cola, unless the act of selling another Joker to make room for it temporarily is a negative act that outweighs the benefits the Double Tag gives. It is recommended to read up on all the [[Tags]] available to see all the potential synergies, as there are too many to list here.

Some particular Jokers that work well with Diet Cola:
* By definition, it is very strong with {{J|Throwback}}, as the player can get even more value out of skipping blinds (though Throwback does not receive additional scaling for each double tag spent).
* Diet Cola very mildly synergizes with {{J|Gift Card}}, as if the player waits a few rounds before selling the cola, they will lose less money overall.
* Selling Diet Cola can also help proc {{J|Campfire}}.
* {{j|Blueprint}} and {{j|Brainstorm}} are compatible with Diet Cola, selling either one while they are copying Diet Cola will also create a Double Tag. This would not be advisable, however, as Blueprint and Brainstorm are far more valuable than the Do
Jokers.strats: * The {{D|Non-Perishable}} [[Challenge Decks|challenge]] bans Diet Cola.

Jokers.effect: If {{hl|orange|first hand}} of round has only {{hl|orange|1}} card, add a permanent copy to deck and draw it to {{hl|orange|hand}}
Jokers.syn:
===[[Decks]]===
*{{D|Blue}} gives an additional hand to play, which can be used to trigger DNA with fewer consequences.
*{{D|Red}} gives an additional discard, which can help in finding a specific card for DNA to copy.
*{{D|Erratic}} starts with uneven ranks and suits, so copying cards with DNA can help further inflate specific ranks/suits, which can allow the player to play higher ranking hands, like {{Ph|Four of a Kind}}, more consistently.

===[[Poker Hands]]===
DNA works best with {{ph|High Card}}, since it requires a High Card on the first hand to trigger.

DNA also works especially well with strong hands that use duplicate cards, like {{ph|Four of a Kind}}, {{ph|Five of a Kind}}, {{ph|Flush Five}}, or {{ph|Flush House}}.

===[[Jokers]]===
*{{J|Hologram}} increases by {{xmult|0.25}} for every card copied by DNA. As a result, DNA can increase Hologram by {{xmult|0.75}} per ante, on top of whatever other cards can be added to your deck.
*{{J|Blue Joker}} adds Chips based on the number of cards in the deck, which can be increased by DNA.
*{{J|Blueprint}} and {{J|Brainstorm}} can be combined with DNA to duplicate a card twice (or thrice if all three Jokers are used together), allowing the player to quickly fill the deck with high value cards. Additionally, it allows the player to immediately use more copies of the card they played. With all three jokers, playing one card will put three copies in hand, for a net of two extra copies available to use.
*{{J|Trading Card}} pairs
Jokers.anti:
===[[Decks]]===
*{{D|Black}}, {{D|Blast Off}}, and {{D|Golden Needle}} all reduce the number of hands to play, which can discourage using DNA while a player's hands aren't strong enough.
** {{D|Golden Needle}} is especially bad, as it only starts with one hand, which means that without a strong High Card build, DNA is unlikely to be a useful purchase.

===[[Poker Hands]]===
DNA is weakest when building for {{ph|Straight}} or {{ph|Straight Flush}}, because it is harder to duplicate cards into runs than it is to duplicate cards into sets.

===[[Jokers]]===
* {{J|Erosion}}'s effect depends on having fewer cards than you started with, and the cards added by DNA make it very difficult to get and stay under that limit.
* Unless with a build around High Cards, triggering DNA will waste one hand per round, which means {{J|Ice Cream}} and {{J|Seltzer}} will be depleted more quickly.
* While {{J|B

Jokers.effect:
{{xmult|3}} if you have at least {{hl|orange|16}} Enhanced cards in your full deck
{{Currently|{{hl|orange|0}}}}
Jokers.unlock: Enhance 16 cards in your deck
Jokers.syn:
===[[Decks]]===
*{{D|Yellow}}: The bonus {{Money|10}} allows for better econ in early to mid game to afford Booster packs.
*{{D|Magic}}: Starting with two copies of {{Tarot|The Fool}}, this can get the player's number of enhanced cards up to 6 at the first shop, nearly half of the required amount to activate Driver's License.
*{{D|Zodiac}}: Increased Tarot cards in shop means more chance to get enhancement cards.
*{{D|Anaglyph}}: Skipping for {{Tag|Charm}}, {{Tag|Ethereal}} or {{Tag|Standard}} can accelerate Driver's License.
*{{D|Fragile}} starts with all 52 cards as {{Enhancement|Glass}}s, meaning that Driver's License will be immediately activated, but be aware if your deck reaches to 15 or less cards.
**On a similar note, {{D|Medusa}} starts with 12 {{Enhancement|Stone}}s and an Eternal {{Sticker|Eternal|image=Marble Joker.png|link=Marble Joker|name=Marble Joker}}, meaning that Driver's License will become active after Round 4

===[[Jokers]]===
*Jokers that add enhanced cards to your deck or change cards into enhanced ones like {{J|Marble Joker}}, {{J|Midas Mask}}, or {{J|DNA}} can help activate Driver's License a lot sooner.
** Combining Midas Mask with {{J|Pareidolia}} is extremely effective for this instance as it can turn all scored cards into {{Enhancement|Gold}}s, activating Driver's License at a record pace.
*{{J|Vagabond}} can also create many enhanced cards very quickly.
*Any Joker that relies on specific enhancements, such as {{J|Lucky Cat}} and {{J|Steel Joker}
Jokers.anti:
===[[Decks]]===
*{{D|Nebula}} works somewhat poorly with Driver's License, as its -1 consumable slot penalty does not allow for many useful consumables to be held at once.
*{{D|Blast Off}} makes Driver's License harder to activate due to the starting {{V|Planet Merchant}} and {{V|Planet Tycoon}} vouchers, which reduce the probabilities of Tarot cards appearing in the shop.

===[[Jokers]]===
*{{J|Vampire}} is not a good Joker to combine with Driver's License, as any played enhanced card will get the enhancement removed and leave Driver's License useless.

===[[Vouchers]]===
*{{V|Planet Merchant}} and {{V|Planet Tycoon}} reduce the probability of Tarot cards appearing in the shop.

Jokers.effect: {{Mult|+10}} if played hand contains a {{ph|Flush}}
Jokers.syn:
===[[Decks]]===
*{{D|Magic}} helps a fair amount in getting flushes, as multiple tarot cards can change a card into a certain suit.
*{{D|Ghost}}, like the Magic Deck, helps as a lot of Spectral cards may help in getting a lot of your cards into one Suit.
*{{D|Checkered}} may be the best deck for this Joker, as flushes are extremely easy due to the deck only containing two suits to start with.
*{{D|Zodiac}} can help you buy tarot cards to change your deck into one suit.
*{{D|Erratic}} can sometimes be extremely good for flushes, depending on the contents of your deck.

===[[Poker hands]]===
This Joker works with {{ph|Flush}} and {{Ph|Straight Flush}} as well as 2 of the hidden hands, {{ph|Flush House}} and {{ph|Flush Five}}.

===[[Jokers]]===
* {{J|Crafty Joker}} and {{J|The Tribe}} always activate at the same time as this Joker.
* {{J|Four Fingers}} and {{J|Smeared Joker}} help in making it easier to create flushes.
* Depending on your deck and which suit you are playing off of, one of the pairs of {{J|Greedy Joker}}/{{J|Rough Gem}}, {{J|Lusty Joker}}/{{J|Bloodstone}}, {{J|Wrathful Joker}}/{{J|Arrowhead}} or {{J|Gluttonous Joker}}/{{J|Onyx Agate}} can work for diamonds, hearts, spades and clubs respectively.
===[[Consumables]]===
[[Tarot cards]]:
*{{Tarot|The Moon}}, {{Tarot|The Star}}, {{Tarot|The Sun}}, and {{Tarot|The World}} turn cards into Clubs, Diamonds, Hearts, and Spades, respectively, which can be useful if the player wants their deck to focus on one or two suits.

Jokers.effect: {{hl|red|+1}} discard each round
Jokers.syn:
===[[Decks]]===
*{{d|Green}} in particular synergizes well as the player earns money for leftover discards.
===[[Poker hands]]===
All hands can benefit from Drunkard, as it makes it easier to search for the desired cards.
===[[Jokers]]===
Drunkard has synergy with:
*Jokers that activate when discarding specific cards, suits, or hands:
**{{j|Trading Card}} when discarding a single card.
**{{j|Hit the Road}} when discarding Jacks.
**{{j|Faceless Joker}} when discarding 3+ face cards.
**{{j|Burnt Joker}} when discarding any Poker Hand.
**{{j|Mail-In Rebate}} when discarding the random rank chosen.
**{{j|Castle}} when discarding the random suit chosen.
*"Remaining discards" Jokers:
**{{j|Banner}} gives more chips if the player has more discards.
**{{j|Delayed Gratification}} provides {{Money|2}} per discard if no discards are used.
*Jokers that want to play a specific, difficult to find hand:
**{{j|Séance}} wants to play a Straight Flush.
**{{j|Superposition}} wants to play a Straight that includes an Ace.
**{{j|Card Sharp}} wants you to play the same Poker Hand twice.
**{{J|The Family}} wants to play a Four of a Kind.
*{{j|Yorick}} to help scale Yorick faster.

===[[Modifiers]]===
*{{Seal|Purple}}: The extra discard provides more opportunities to generate more Tarot cards.

===[[Stakes]]===
*Drunkard restores a discard lost from playing {{Stake|Blue}} and above.
Jokers.anti:
===Jokers===
*{{j|Burglar}} as it removes all discards (no matter the order of the 2 Jokers).
*{{j|Green Joker}} as it gets {{Mult|-1}} for every discard used.
*{{j|Ramen}} as any discard reduces its {{Xmult|}}.

===Blinds===
*{{Blind|The Water}} will always set your discards to 0, making Drunkard useless.

Jokers.effect: Retrigger all played cards in {{hl|orange|final hand}} of the round
Jokers.syn:
===[[Decks]]===
* {{D|Black}} reduces the available Hands for the player by -1, making it less punishing for the player to use their final hand.
*Similarly, {{D|Blast Off}} reduces the available Hands for the player by -2, making it less punishing for the player to use their final hand.
*{{D|Golden Needle}} reduces the player's Hands to 1, meaning Dusk is automatically activated.
===[[Poker hands]]===
Dusk works best with five card hands, such as {{ph|Flushes}} and {{ph|Straights}}, due to these giving Dusk more cards to retrigger, thus giving a higher score.
=== [[Jokers]]===
* Dusk synergizes well with {{j|Hack}} when playing low-ranked cards, as they allow each card to be triggered three times.
* Similarly to Hack, {{J|Sock and Buskin}} synergizes well with Dusk, as it allows face cards to be triggered more.
* {{j|Acrobat}} is a good pair with Dusk, provided players have a lot of Mult cards and {{Hl|Red|+Mult}} Jokers ready for the final hand.
* {{J|Troubadour}}'s -1 Hand penalty becomes mostly irrelevant as Dusk only activates on the final hand.
* As with all retrigger Jokers, any Joker that cares about certain cards being scored goes well with Dusk. Notable examples are {{J|Bloodstone}} and {{J|Triboulet}}, as their {{xmult|}} effects stack.
* {{J|Hiker}} has incredible synergy with Dusk, as not only will Hiker scale cards twice as fast, but the retriggering of the cards will also give their chips again.
* {{J|Lucky Cat}} can scale twice as fast since the {{enhancement|L
Jokers.anti:
===Decks===
*{{D|Green}} gives no interest, instead gaining {{Money|2}}/Hand and {{Money|1}}/Discard remaining. Using all your hands to trigger Dusk means losing most of your income.
===Jokers===
*Dusk will deplete {{j|Seltzer}} and {{j|Ice Cream}} faster, as Dusk requires the player to exhaust all hands to trigger.
===Blinds===
*If {{Blind|Crimson Heart}} debuffs Dusk on the final hand, it cannot retrigger any card.

Jokers.effect: Gains {{Money|3}} of {{Hl|orange|sell value}} at end of round
Jokers.syn:
===[[Decks]]===
The {{D|Green}} cannot generate interest, and can especially benefit from alternative income sources like Egg.
===[[Poker hands]]===
This Joker does not add Chips or Mult, so no hand benefits or suffers from it.
===[[Jokers]]===
*{{J|Swashbuckler}} can combo with Egg to gain Mult each round, but will lose it if Egg is sold. While Debuffed, Egg will still provide Mult for Swashbuckler.
*{{J|Ceremonial Dagger}} can be used to sacrifice Egg for a permanent Mult bonus.
===[[Tarot cards]]===
*The money given by {{Tarot|Temperance}} scales with the sell value of the player's Jokers. The longer players have Egg, the more money they'll get from Temperance, even potentially hitting the maximum value of {{Money|50}} they can get from the Tarot card.
===[[Vouchers]]===
*{{V|Hieroglyph}} and {{V|Petroglyph}} send the player back an [[Ante]], giving players more time to scale Egg's sell value.
Jokers.anti:
===[[Decks]]===
* {{D|Anaglyph}} incentives skipping blinds due to its {{Tag|Double}} gimmick, which gives Egg less chances to increase its sell value.
* Since {{D|Painted}} and {{D|Blast Off}} only have 4 Joker slots instead of the typical 5, taking Egg is much more risky since it doesn't immediately help the player score and its only purpose is to be sold.
* {{D|Cruelty}} makes it even more difficult and risky to use Egg, as this deck only has 3 Joker slots.
*{{D|Non-Perishable}} makes every Joker {{Sticker|Eternal}}, including Egg, which means it cannot be sold.

===[[Jokers]]===
*{{J|Throwback}} encourages skipping blinds to scale the {{XMult|}} of the Joker, once again giving Egg less opportunity to increase its sell value.
===[[Stakes]]===
*On {{Stake|Black}} and above, there is a chance for an Egg to be {{Sticker|Eternal}}, which makes it impossible to sell if picked up, nullifyin
Jokers.strats: * {{D|The Omelette}} challenge starts the player with 5 copies of Egg.

Jokers.effect:
{{Mult|+4}} for each card below {{hl|orange|[the deck's starting size]}} in your full deck
{{Currently|{{Mult|+0}}}}
Jokers.syn:
===[[Decks]]===
Erosion has synergy with all decks, since most players generally want to reduce their deck size anyway in order to draw more reliably. However, it is especially powerful when used with these decks:
* {{D|Zodiac}} can provide more [[Tarot cards]] in the [[The Shop|Shop]] with its starting {{V|Tarot Merchant}}, potentially increasing the odds of getting {{Tarot|The Hanged Man}}.
* {{D|Ghost}} allows for [[Spectral cards]] to appear in [[the Shop]], which can potentially include {{Spectral|Immolate}}.
* Erosion works extremely well on {{d|Fragile}}, as the player starts with a 52 card deck full of {{Enhancement|Glass}}s that are guaranteed to break by virtue of having 2 {{j|Oops! All 6s}} upon starting the challenge.

===[[Poker hands]]===
If the player can choose which cards to destroy, it may be useful to build towards higher-scoring hands, such as {{Ph|Four of a Kind}} or {{Ph|Full House}}. If not, it may be best to focus on smaller hands, such as {{Ph|Two Pair}} or {{Ph|Three of a Kind}}.

===[[Jokers]]===
* {{J|Trading Card}} is able to destroy one card once per round giving Erosion {{Mult|+4}} each time.
* {{J|Sixth Sense}} can destroy a 6 once per round, and potentially provide an {{Spectral|Immolate}} card.
* [[Tarot cards|Tarot]] generating Jokers like {{J|Cartomancer}} or {{J|Vagabond}} can give access to {{Tarot|The Hanged Man}} and {{Tarot|Justice}}, or {{Tarot|The Fool}} to copy them.
* {{J|Glass Joker}} gains {{xmult|0.75}} every time a {{Enhancemen
Jokers.anti:

* {{D|Abandoned}} might have anti-synergy with Erosion, as it has only 40 cards instead of 52. Since there are less cards, erosion has a lower ceiling on the maximum mult it can give.
* {{d|Mad World}} starts with a 32 card deck, making it extremely difficult to earn value from Erosion with a ceiling even lower than the {{d|Abandoned}}.
* {{D|Medusa}} and {{D|Monolith}} don't work well with Erosion, as these decks both start with an [[Eternal]] {{Sticker|Eternal|image=Marble Joker.png|link=Marble Joker|name=Marble Joker}}, which makes Erosion very hard to scale.

===Jokers===
* {{J|Blue Joker}} gives additional {{Chips|+}} based on the size of player's deck, so it will provide less benefit as the player reduces their deck size for Erosion.
* Jokers that add playing cards to the player's deck reduce the amount of {{Mult|+}} Erosion can provide.
** This includes: {{J|Certificat

Jokers.effect:
Played cards with [[Card Ranks|{{hl|orange|even}}]] rank give {{Mult|+4}} when scored
{{hl|gray|(10, 8, 6, 4, 2)}}
Jokers.syn:
Even Steven is a decent source of {{hl|red|+Mult}} that triggers through cards, effectively being {{mult|+20}} if all played cards are even and trigger once. It works very well as an early-game source of Mult, but can fall off unless heavily built around (and even then, it isn't the best Joker to build around).

===[[Decks]]===
*{{d|Abandoned}} works very well with Steven, since it allows the player to find even ranks more easily. It makes even cards about 20% more common to draw (in an unaltered deck).
*{{D|Mad World}} will also work as well, although this deck doesn't start with any 10s.
*{{d|Magic}}'s Fools can be used to turn many odd cards into evens with {{Tarot|Strength}}s, or copy a strong even card with {{Tarot|Death}}s.

===[[Poker hands]]===
Steven works best with hands that play five even cards. This is mainly {{Ph|Full House}}, though {{Ph|Four of a Kind}} may work well with its higher base chips, and later {{Ph|Five of a Kind}}. {{Ph|Flushes}} can serve as a decent alternative, since they can be easier to find and will still (ideally) contain some even cards.

===[[Jokers]]===
Even Steven is, in essence, a more effective version of the sinful Jokers (the ones that give +3 Mult per scored card of a certain suit). In an unaltered deck, the chance an even card is drawn is ~38%, compared to the 25% of a specific suit, and it gives more Mult. In exchange, it's harder to build around since there are fewer rank-changing methods than suit changers, and it can be harder

Jokers.effect: Earn {{Money|5}} if {{hl|orange|3}} or more {{hl|orange|face cards}} are discarded at the same time
Jokers.syn:
===[[Decks]]===
*{{d|Red}} gives +1 Discard, allowing more chances to discard and dig for face cards.
*{{D|Golden Needle}} removes money when discarding, and Faceless Joker is an effective counter to this.

===[[Poker hands]]===
Because this Joker requires discarding face cards, which provide lots of Chips, it's recommended to build toward weaker hands like {{ph|High Card}}, {{ph|Pair}}, or {{ph|Two Pair}}.
===[[Jokers]]===
*{{j|Pareidolia}} makes it so that all cards are considered face cards, effectively guaranteeing {{Money|5}} per every 3 cards discarded.
*{{j|Drunkard}} gives +1 Discard, allowing more chances to find and discard face cards.
*{{j|Merry Andy}} gives +3 Discards, allowing more chances to find and discard face cards.
*{{J|Blueprint}} and {{J|Brainstorm}} can copy Faceless Joker to effectively double/triple amount of money gained with no downside as they can be moved around to buff scoring Jokers afterward.
===[[Vouchers]]===
*{{V|Wasteful}} and {{v|Recyclomancy}} give additional discards, allowing more chances to find and discard face cards.
Jokers.anti:
===[[Decks]]===
*{{d|Abandoned}} and {{D|Medusa}} start with no face cards, making Faceless Joker useless at the beginning unless paired with {{j|Pareidolia}}.
*{{D|Blast Off}} doesn't work well with Faceless Joker, as this deck only starts with 2 discards.

===[[Jokers]]===
*Jokers that benefit from playing or keeping face cards, such as {{J|Scary Face}} or {{J|Baron}}, are worse as Faceless Joker incentivizes discarding face cards. Possible exceptions are if {{J|Pareidolia}} is used or if the deck is heavily manipulated for face cards.
*Any Jokers that benefit from not using Discards like {{J|Delayed Gratification}} or {{J|Banner}} have anti-synergy with Faceless Joker.
*{{J|Burglar}} removes all discards, effectively disabling Faceless Joker.
===[[Blinds]]===
*{{Blind|The Water}} starts with 0 discards, making Faceless Joker useless for the round.

* {{D|Ghost}}: This Deck has easier access to the {{Spectral|Wraith}} Spectral card, which serves as a higher-risk but higher-reward version of the aforementioned {{Tarot|Judgement}}. ===[[Poker hands]]===
Luchador doesn't benefit any poker hands directly. However, certain hands can occasionally appreciate the assistance it provides (such as {{Ph|Flush}} against one of the suit-debuffing Boss Blinds, or, less frequently, a {{Ph|High Card}}/{{Ph|Pair}}/{{Ph|Three of a Kind}} build against {{blind|The Psychic}}).

===[[Jokers]]===
Being a utility Joker, Luchador does not directly synergize with any build. However, it can enable a wealth of Jokers that are otherwise soft or hard countered by specific Boss Blinds, in the event they are encountered.

*
Jokers.anti:

===[[Boss Blinds]]===
* {{Blind|Amber Acorn}} flips and shuffles all Jokers, so the player doesn't know which of their Jokers is Luchador. Trying to pick a Joker to sell could likely result in selling the wrong card by mistake.

Jokers.strats:
{{trim|{{#lst:Mr. Bones|bbl}}}}
In fact, for most runs, players are only vulnerable to 1-2 specific Boss Blinds and one Showdown Blind. In an Ante 8 run, excluding Ante 1 and 2 (at which point a specific gameplay style is unlikely to be formed), the probability of encountering both detrimental Boss Blinds, or a Boss Blind combined with a Showdown Blind is relatively low (both around 6%). Therefore, Luchador is sufficient to handle the risk. However, in endless mode, the player will face many Boss Blinds, so it would be better to have a method that can avoid multiple Boss Blinds (such as {{J|Chicot}} and {{V|Director's Cut}}).

Copying Mail-In Rebate with {{J|Blueprint}} or {{J|Brainstorm}} while discarding 5 cards gives a total of $50, and adding more copies just adds more money per discard.

The player should be careful not to discard too much, as completely running out of cards is an instant loss.

*{{D|Painted}} allows the player to have more cards in hand, letting the player discard more cards without sacrificing good hands.
*{{D|Black}} can more easily take Mail-In Rebate, as it has more Joker slots, and it is recommended to discard more with Black Deck anyway, as the player must play better hands to compensate for having fewer hands. Black Deck can also hold more Jokers that help with discarding, like {{J|Drunkard}}.
*{{D|Abandoned}} and {{D|Mad World}} both contain fewer ranks and total cards, making it easier to find the selected rank and discard it.
*{{D|Golden Needle}} removes money when discarding, and Mail-In Rebate is an effective counter to this.

===[[Poker Hands]]===
Hands that need fewer cards are better if the player has a smaller hand size, like {{Ph|Three of a Kind}}, which allows them to discard 5 cards if they have the default hand size. For this reason, {{Ph|Straight}}, {{Ph|Flush}}, and {{Ph|Full House}} are less valuable with Rebate.

However, {{Ph|Five of a Kind}} and {{Ph|Flush Five}} are ''sometimes'' better in highly centralized decks, as with more of that rank, Mail-In Rebate will likely choose that rank, and discarding them will be fine, as the player is more likely to draw more to form a Five of a Kind still.

*Jokers that add more discards work great with Mail-In Rebate, those being {{J|Drunkard}} and {{J|Merry And

*Any Jokers that benefits from not using Discards, like {{J|Delayed Gratification}} or {{J|Banner}}, have anti-synergy with Mail-In Rebate.
*{{J|Burglar}} removes all discards, effectively disabling Mail-In Rebate.

=== [[Blinds]] ===
*{{Blind|The Water}} sets your discards to 0, making Mail-In Rebate useless for the round.
*Since debuffed cards do not have a rank, any blind that debuffs cards makes it less likely for the player to make use of Mail-In Rebate.

*{{Stake|Blue}} and above hinder Mail-In Rebate's potential because they have 1 less discard by default.

However, the Stone cards it adds can end up supplanting a Chips Joker entirely, meaning you can sell Marble after getting value from it and go into the final Boss Blind with an extra Mult or effect Joker you'd be missing otherwise. With that said, Marble joker can be great when it's fueling some specific other jokers.

* {{D|Red}}'s extra discards, {{D|Painted}}'s higher hand size, and {{D|Abandoned}}'s smaller deck size all allow the player to find more unique hands, which helps with keeping the {{XMult|}} on Obelisk without risking playing the most played hand. Painted Deck also appreciates having such a high-value {{XMult|}} Joker.
* {{D|Blue}}'s extra hands allow Obelisk to scale faster per round.

It also helps the player after pivoting if the build does not revolve around {{ph|Flush}} beforehand, as having another hand type that's easy to hit reduces the chance of resetting Obelisk accidentally.

===[[Poker hands]]===
No particular poker hand is better with Obelisk. The {{ph|Pair}} or {{ph| Two Pair}} strategy mentioned below could be considered a synergy, but the bulk of the game will be spent playing as many different hands as possible to keep options open in the future.

===[[Jokers]]===
*Jokers that produce Mult without hand-based conditions are what you always want to use with Obelisk. These can be flat {{Mult|+}} Jokers, like {{J|Fibonacci}} and {{J|Gros Michel}}, but the most success comes from scaling ones, like {{J|Bootstraps}}, {{J|Erosion}}, {{J|Ride the Bus}}, or {{J|Fortune Teller}}. Having one of these scaling Jokers

===Jokers===

Obelisk can become a very powerful Scaling {{XMult|}} Joker, but it cannot be used in every build. It works best on builds that don't rely on playing specific hands to score, as if too many of any one hand are played, you can no longer play it without resetting the Obelisk.

The most effective strategy with Obelisk is to play {{ph|Pair}} or {{ph|Two Pair}} until around 15 have been played, then pivoting in the later antes to playing any other hand. It is not recommended to use Obelisk if the most played hand is {{ph|High Card}}, as the player runs a higher risk of being forced to reset the Obelisk.

These include the {{d|Painted}} (+2 hand size), the {{d|Checkered}} (only {{Suit|Hearts}} and {{Suit|Spades}}), and especially the {{d|Abandoned}} (no face cards), which can very easily leverage the fast scaling of {{ph|Straight}}s with the {{Planet|Saturn}} [[Planet card]] in tandem with this Joker. Even certain {{d|Erratic}} seeds can lend themselves well to consistently finding high-performing hands.

===[[Poker hands]]===
This Joker works best with weaker hands that can be more reliably made without discarding (or by using a hand as a makeshift discard), such as {{ph|High Card}}, {{ph|Pair}}, {{ph|Two Pair}}, and {{ph|Three of a Kind}}. To that end, this will force the player to become more dependent on Planet card scaling than wit
Jokers.anti:
===Decks===
* {{d|Red}}: This Deck has anti-synergy with this Joker, as it encourages the player to discard more to find better hands.
* {{d|Black}} makes it very difficult to use Ramen, as it suffers from -1 hand per round. This forces more dependency on discards while disallowing liberal use of 'throwaway' hands.
**Similarly, {{D|Blast Off}} makes it even more difficult to use Ramen, as this deck only has 2 hands. This forces much more dependency on discards while disallowing liberal use of 'throwaway' hands.

===Jokers===
* {{j|Drunkard}} and {{j|Merry Andy}}: The extra discards these two provide are almost useless in a Ramen build, except when considering the potential presence of {{j|Banner}} or {{j|Delayed Gratification}}. Using 3 Joker slots for such
Jokers.strats: * The {{D|Non-Perishable}} [[Challenge Decks|challenge]] bans Ramen.

Jokers.effect:
This Joker gains {{Mult|+3}} when any [[Booster Packs|{{hl|orange|Booster Pack}}]] is skipped
{{Currently|{{mult|+0}}}}
Jokers.syn:
===[[Decks]]===
*{{d|Anaglyph}} can build up many tags, then copy any tag that gives a Mega Booster Pack.
*{{d|Green}} encourages the player to spend money as they earn it, which works well with Red Card.
*In {{d|Typecast}}, after Ante 4, {{Booster|Buffoon}}s will continue to spawn in the shop despite it being impossible to take Jokers from them. Red Card can be used to extract value from what would otherwise be a wasted booster slot.
===[[Jokers]]===
*Red Card synergizes well with most economy Jokers that provide money, like {{j|Business Card}} or {{j|Rocket}}.
*{{J|Astronomer}} can provide free {{Booster|Celestial}}s that can be used to scale.
*{{J|Hallucination}} can allow you to still get tarot cards even while skipping packs.

=== [[Vouchers]] ===
*{{V|Clearance Sale}} and {{V|Liquidation}} lower the price of booster packs, making it easier to purchase and skip more.
*{{V|Hieroglyph}} and {{V|Petroglyph}} send the player back an [[Ante]] at the cost of -1 Hand and -1 Discard respectively, allowing them to open more booster packs to skip.

=== [[Tags]] ===
Skipping for these Tags works best when the player is on the {{d|Anaglyph}} or has taken lots of {{J|Diet Cola}}s.
*{{Tag|Standard}}, {{Tag|Charm}}, {{Tag|Meteor}} and {{Tag|Buffoon}} all give access to Mega Booster Packs, which can be used by taking 1 card, then skipping to scale Red Card.
*{{Tag|Ethereal}} gives access to a Spectral Pack, which can optionally be skipped to scale Red Card.
Jokers.anti:
There are a lot of Jokers that, when combined with Red Card, leave the player in a dilemma between whether to scale Red Card or whether to scale the other joker. However, it is worth emphasizing again that skipping a Booster Pack ''specifically'' to scale up Red Card (instead of skipping a Booster Pack that already had very little value) might not be a good idea. Moreover, it is debatable whether these are true anti-synergies (rather than complements), since pairing the Red Card with any of these lessens the punishment of opening Booster Packs that don't have what you want:
*Jokers that care about Tarot cards, such as {{J|Fortune Teller}}, {{J|Driver's License}}, and {{J|Vampire}}.
*Jokers such as {{J|Steel Joker}} and {{J|Lucky Cat}}, which care about specific Tarot cards.
*Jokers that care about Planet cards, such as {{J|Constellation}} and {{J|Satellite}}.
*As for {{Booster|Standard}}
Jokers.strats:
When playing with Red Card, it's better not to skip Booster Packs ''specifically'' just to scale the Red Card. Opening a Booster Pack is more like rolling for a chance to get a good item — Booster Packs are not guaranteed to provide value, and the player would skip many Booster Packs anyway due to not getting a card that is sufficiently valuable. What Red Card does is that it provides {{Mult|+3}} in all of the cases where the player would have skipped anyway, so it is better to think of Red Card as an additional Booster Pack slot and to only skip if none of the options are better than +3 mult.

For instance, with 9 [[Planet cards]] available at the beginning of a run and three of those being visible in a regular {{Booster|Celestial}}, assuming no Telescope, there is only a 1 in 3 chance for a Celestial Pack to contain the Planet card that one actually wants. The other two-thirds of the time, the player would just skip or take a Planet card of an undesirable hand, gaining little to no value out of it. But with the Red Card, the player would get a minimum of {{Mult|+3}} — it might be more reasonable to think of it as a fourth Planet card that gives {{Mult|+3}} for every hand (assuming no {{XMult|}} triggered on played or held cards).

If the player opens a Mega Booster Pack, the player can still use the first card and then skip to scale up Red Card.

*{{j|Shoot the Moon}} also wants the player to keep face cards (Queen) in hand.
*{{j|Baron}} also wants the player to keep face cards (King) in hand.
*{{j|Ride the Bus}} also does not want to play face cards. Note that having these 2 jokers at the same time can be very dangerous, as there's a small chance of drawing a hand of only face cards.
*{{j|Juggler}} and {{j|Troubadour}} increase hand size, allowing the player to hold more cards in hand.
*{{j|Burglar}} gives 3 extra hands, allowing more chances for Reserved Parking to give more money.

===[[Modifier
Jokers.anti:
===[[Decks]]===
*{{D|Abandoned}} and {{D|Medusa}} start with no face cards, meaning Reserved Parking Joker is useless.
*{{D|Black}}, {{D|Blast Off}}, and {{D|Golden Needle}} all have fewer hands to be used for yielding money.
*{{D|Five-Card Draw}} does not work well with this Joker due to the decreased hand size and banning of hand size-increasing Jokers.

===[[Poker hands]]===
Five-card hands like {{Ph|Flush}}, {{Ph|Straight}} or {{Ph|Full House}} leaves fewer cards held in hand so it doesn't benefit Reserved Parking much.

===[[Jokers]]===
*{{J|Merry Andy}} and {{J|Stuntman}} reduce hand sizes, which means the player hold less face cards.
*{{J|Faceless Joker}} encourages discarding lots of face cards.
*{{J|Canio}} encourages destroying face cards.
*{{J|Business Card}} encourages playing face cards instead, although this could actually be a synergy if the player has a lot of face cards
Jokers.strats:
Reserved Parking rolls a {{hl|green|1 in 2}} on each face card held in hand, so the expected value per face card per hand is {{Money|0.5}}. {{j|Mime}} and {{Seal|Red|name=Red Seals|image=King of Spades.png}} will only attempt to retrigger this effect if the initial roll was successful. As a result, one retrigger will raise the expected value to {{Money|0.75}} per card per hand, and two retriggers raises the expected value to {{Money|1}}.

If the player also already has another held in hand effect that triggers on every hand, like {{j|Baron}}, {{j|Shoot the Moon}} or {{Enhancement|Steel}}s, then {{j|Mime}} and {{Seal|Red|name=Red Seals|image=King of Spades.png}} will always retrigger this effect, and therefore this card. As a result, Reserved Parking can be retriggered even if the initial roll was unsuccessful. In this case, one retrigger raises expected value to {{Money|1}} per hand, two retriggers raises expected value to {{Money|1.5}}.
