*{{d|Painted}} with its increased Hand Size, can make Straights easier to form with more cards held in hand.
*{{d|Plasma}} significantly benefits from early Chips value. This makes Runner an easy choice for the early to mid game, although it can be carried into late game if the player builds around Straights.
*{{D|15 Minute City}} starts with an Eternal {{Sticker|Eternal|image=Shortcut.png|link=Shortcut|name=Shortcut}}, which allows Straights to be made with gaps in them, making it easier to get that hand.

===[[Poker hands]]===
*{{ph|Straight}}, {{ph|Straight Flush}}, and {{ph|Royal Flush}} are recommended to scale Runner consistently.

===[[Jokers]]===
*{{j|Shortcut}} allows Straights to be made with gaps in them, making it easier to get that hand.
*{{j|Four Fingers}} allows Straights to be scored with only four cards instead of the usual five, making it easier to get that hand.
*{{j|The Order}} will give {{xmult|3}} as long as the played hand contains a Straight, making it a strong partner with Runner for both scaling Chips and XMult.
*{{j|Crazy Joker}} gives {{mult|+12}} on Straights, being especially useful to increase Mult during the early game.
===[[Vouchers]]===
*{{V|Grabber}} and {{v|Nacho Tong}} give additional hands, allowing Runner to scale faster.
*{{V|Wasteful}} and {{v|Recyclomancy}} give additional discards
Jokers.anti:
===[[Decks]]===
*{{D|Black}}, {{D|Blast Off}}, and {{D|Golden Needle}} all have poor synergy with Runner due to their reduced number of hands.
*{{d|Erratic}} can make it difficult to use Runner as the randomized rank and suit makes it harder to form Straights.
*{{D|Five-Card Draw}}'s -3 hand size makes it extremely hard to assemble Straights.

===[[Jokers]]===
*Jokers that reduce hand size, like {{j|Stuntman}} and {{j|Merry Andy}}, have anti-synergy with Runner, as a smaller hand size makes it harder to assemble Straights.

===[[Consumables]]===
*{{Spectral|Ectoplasm}} and {{Spectral|Ouija}} have anti-synergy with Runner, as a smaller hand size makes it harder to assemble Straights. Not only that, but {{Spectral|Ouija}} converts all cards held in hand into one single rank, which makes assembling Straights less consistent.

===[[Blinds and Antes|Blinds]]===
*{{Blind|The Manacle}}'s -1 han

Jokers.effect: Earn {{Money|1}} at end of round per unique {{hl|cyan|Planet}} card used this run
Jokers.unlock: Have at least {{Money|400}}.
Jokers.syn:
===[[Decks]]===
* {{D|Checkered}} works well with Satellite as it requires fewer Deck modifications to unlock the secret Poker hands.
* {{D|Erratic}} may require no Deck modifications at all to unlock the secret Poker hands.

===[[Poker hands]]===
Playing the three secret hands ({{Ph|Flush House}}, {{Ph|Five of a Kind}} and {{Ph|Flush Five}}) to unlock their planets allows players to maximize this Joker's value.
===[[Jokers]]===
* Since Satellite is maximized through the use of Planet cards, it synergizes with {{J|Constellation}}, which gains {{Xmult|0.1}} per planet card used.
* Satellite benefits from {{J|Astronomer}}, which makes planet cards and Celestial booster packs free.
* {{J|Smeared Joker}} can make it much easier to unlock the secret hands, thereby maximizing Satellite's value.

===[[Consumables]]===
*{{Tarot|The High Priestess}} can potentially spawn Planet cards not yet used by the player if found early, boosting Satellite.

===[[Vouchers]]===
* {{v|Planet Merchant}} and {{v|Planet Tycoon}} increase the frequency of planet cards in the shop, making it easier to find different planet cards.
Jokers.anti:
===Jokers===
* {{J|Showman}} can have anti-synergy with Satellite, since it will allow duplicate planet cards to appear, and Satellite requires unique planet cards.
===Vouchers===
* {{v|Telescope}} can make it harder to achieve max rewards with Satellite, as it lends itself to the same planet card repeating.
** This innately applies to the {{D|Nebula}} as it starts with the Telescope Voucher.
Jokers.strats:
Without a steady Economy, unlocking Satellite may prove to be a difficult task.
* The {{D|Yellow}} is a decent choice for the run to unlock Satellite as it starts the player with an extra {{money|10}}, earning the player Interest from defeating the first Blind of the run, and setting up for further Economic gain.
* Economy Jokers such as {{J|Golden Joker}}, {{J|Mail-In Rebate}}, etc. are directly helpful in reaching the unlock condition.
* The {{J|Bull}} and {{J|Bootstraps}} Jokers both gain scoring power relative to the player's Money, which would be useful to have in a run that attempts to unlock Satellite as hoarding Money to reach {{money|400}} will also give it scoring power.
* {{J|Egg}} and {{J|Gift Card}} add sell value, making it possible to hold onto the Egg or a useless Joker/Consumable to sell later for a substantial boost in Money.
** {{J|Swashbuckler}} would quantify the sell value into Mult, which may help the player continue the run.
* {{J|To the Moon}}, {{V|Seed Money}}, and {{V|Money Tree}} allow the player to earn more Interest, which may contribute to reaching the unlock condition faster.
** All 3 of these combined allow for the player to earn a maximum of {{money|40}} from Interest alone, merely one-tenth of the required amount.
* {{D|The Omelette}} [[Challenge Decks|challenge]] bans Satellite.

Jokers.effect: Played {{hl|orange|face}} cards give {{Chips|+30}} when scored

===[[Poker hands]]===

===[[Jokers]]===
*If the first card of the hand is a face card, {{J|Hanging Chad}} will cause Scary Face to trigger thrice, giving {{chips|+90}}.
*{{j|Pareidolia}} causes Scary Face to trigger on all played cards, effectively making every card a {{Enhancement|Bonus}}.
*{{j|Sock and Buskin}} will add an additional {{Chips|+30}} per face card scored.
*{{j|Triboulet}} provides a Mult multiplier for each played King or Queen.
*{{j|Business Card}} gives each face card played a 50% chance to provide {{Money|2}} when scored.
*{{j|Smiley Face}} provides additional Mult for each face card played.
*{{j|Splash}} allows non-scoring cards to trigger Scary Face (by maki

*{{j|Baron}}, {{J|Shoot the Moon}}, {{J|Hit the Road}} and {{j|Reserved Parking}} encourage not playing face cards.

Jokers.effect: Played {{hl|orange|Aces}} give {{chips|+20}} and {{mult|+4}} when scored
Jokers.syn:
===[[Decks]]===
*{{D|Abandoned}} can reliably find Aces more often than the typical 52-card decks.
*{{D|Red}} gives +1 discard, allowing for more opportunities to dig for Aces.

===[[Poker hands]]=== 
*{{Ph|Pair}} of Aces
*{{Ph|Three of a Kind}} with Aces
*{{Ph|Four of a Kind}} with Aces
*{{Ph|Five of a Kind}} with Aces
*{{Ph|Flush Five}} with Aces
*{{Ph|Straight}} or {{Ph|Straight Flush}} with 5-4-3-2-A or A-K-Q-J-10
*{{Ph|Full House}} with 2 or 3 Aces
*{{Ph|Flush House}} with 2 or 3 Aces
*In general, the more Aces you play in a hand, the more valuable Scholar will be.

*{{J|Fibonacci}} gives you {{Mult|+8}} per Ace.

Jokers.effect: {{xmult|2}} if played hand has a scoring {{suit|Club}} card and a scoring card of any other suit
Jokers.unlock: Play a hand that contains {{hl|orange|four}} <abbr title="Other suits that count as clubs (e.g. wild suits) with rank 7 will also count.">{{hl|orange|7 of Clubs}}</abbr>
Jokers.syn:
===[[Decks]]===
*{{D|Erratic}} may start with more Clubs than a standard deck, and allows for more {{Ph|X of a Kind}}, like {{Ph|Pair}} or {{Ph|Three of a Kind}}, to be played, which could activate Seeing Double's condition more easily.

===[[Poker hands]]===
*{{Ph|Straight}} and {{ph|Full House}} both generate {{xmult|2}} a large majority of the time, making Seeing Double great for those strategies.

===[[Jokers]]===
*{{J|Smeared Joker}} means {{Suit|Clubs}} can also count as {{Suit|Spades}} and vice-versa. This means that playing any hand (even High Card) containing a Club or Spade will trigger Seeing Double.
** This interaction is a [[bug]]. This interaction doesn't apply if the card is {{Enhancement|Wild|name=Wild}}.
*{{J|Splash}} allows triggering the bonus by adding an extra card that would otherwise be ineligible for scoring; e.g. ♣️A ♣️A ♣️A ♣️A ♥️4.
*Almost any hand that triggers {{J|Flower Pot}} will also trigger Seeing Double, providing a total of {{xmult|6}}.
**If some cards are [[debuffed]], {{j|Flower Pot}} may trigger without Seeing Double, as Seeing Double requires at least 1 non debuffed {{suit|Club}} and at least 1 non debuffed non {{suit|Club}}, while {{j|Flower Pot}} still counts debuffed cards.

===[[Card modifiers]]===
*{{enhancement|Wild}}s can count as either the Club or the non-Club, but not both. Generally this means adding any second scoring card (including a second Wild card) will trigger the bonus, though {{Enhancement|Stone}}s will not qualify, h
Jokers.anti:
===Decks===
*{{D|Checkered}} makes it significantly harder to activate Seeing Double, as it contains no Club cards naturally.

===Poker hands===
*{{ph|Flush}}-based hands are hard to use, requiring a {{Enhancement|Wild}}, {{J|Smeared Joker}} or an off-suit card via {{J|Four Fingers}} and {{J|Splash}}.

===[[Blinds]]===
*{{Blind|The Club}} renders Seeing Double useless, as all Club cards are debuffed and debuffed Club cards will not trigger Seeing Double.
*{{Blind|The Pillar}} can make Seeing Double difficult to trigger if players already played some Club cards in the previous round, making them debuffed upon facing this boss blind. This can be remedied by carrying Tarot cards that provide enhancements into the boss blind to "revive" debuffed Club cards.
Jokers.strats:
Unlocking Seeing Double may prove to be challenging at first due to its condition being oddly specific towards a specific rank and suit. In particular, there are no Jokers that directly have synergies with 7s, the sole exception being {{J|Odd Todd}}. Here are some approaches that can help with unlocking Seeing Double:
*{{D|Magic}} starts with two copies of {{tarot|The Fool}}, allowing the player to copy Tarots to make more 7 of Clubs, such as {{tarot|Death}}, {{tarot|The Moon}}, {{tarot|Strength}}, or even {{tarot|The Lovers}}.
*{{D|Erratic}} can generate with more 7 of Clubs from the start.
*{{Enhancement|Wild|name=Wild 7s}} of any suit and 7s of {{Suit|Spades}} with {{J|Smeared Joker}} can also be used.

Jokers.effect: Retrigger all cards played for the next {{hl|orange|10}} hands
Jokers.syn:
===[[Decks]]===
*{{d|Zodiac}} is helpful for finding tarot cards to make the enhanced cards that make Seltzer work effectively.
*{{d|Red}} is able to find better hands on average, so Seltzer will last longer, as less hands need to be played per round.
*{{d|Black}} is able to stack more Jokers that benefit from Seltzer's effect. Adding even a single {{xMult|}} Joker like {{J|Ancient Joker}} can be an extra {{xMult|7.5}} normally, but with Seltzer it becomes an extra {{Xmult|57}}.
*{{d|Plasma}} gains a huge boost from stacking {{xMult|}} modifiers, which Seltzer enables very well.

===[[Poker hands]]===
Any 5-card hands like {{ph|Flush}}, {{ph|Straight}}, or {{ph|Full House}} will provide more retriggers from Seltzer. In particular, {{ph|Flush Fives}}, with five of the same very strong duplicated card, work very well.

===[[Jokers]]===
*Any Joker that triggers on scoring will have its effect doubled, for instance {{J|Scary Face}} for {{Hl|Blue|Chips}}, {{J|Fibonacci}} for {{Hl|Red|+Mult}}, {{J|The Idol}} for {{xMult|}}, or {{J|Rough Gem}} for money.
*Jokers that ''scale'' based on cards played, like {{J|Lucky Cat}} and {{J|Hiker}}, work very well with Seltzer, as the cards they scale with will always retrigger, and the scaling will remain after Seltzer is consumed.
*Jokers like {{J|8 Ball}} (in particular, due to its on scoring nature) and {{J|Cartomancer}} can provide frequent Tarot cards to buff up playing cards.
*{{J|Throwback}} rewards you for skipping blinds, making Seltze
Jokers.anti:
===[[Jokers]]===
* Copying cards with {{J|DNA}} will quickly use up Seltzer's retriggers.
** Similarly, destroying 6s with {{J|Sixth Sense}} will also quickly use up Seltzer's retriggers.
* Jokers that incentivize playing many hands per round, such as {{J|Green Joker}} or {{J|Vagabond}}, will similarly cause Seltzer to be spent quickly.
* Using {{J|Burglar}} does not always guarantee winning in one hand, so the player will have to play hands as pseudo-discards, which will quickly deplete Seltzer.

===Boss Blinds===
*If a hand that is not allowed is played during {{Blind|The Psychic}}, {{Blind|The Mouth}} or {{Blind|The Eye}}, Seltzer will still lose a retrigger.
Jokers.strats: In a build with many enhanced cards, Seltzer can be a powerful joker, especially in the late game. Due to Seltzer's limited lifespan, it is often used to get the highest scoring single hand possible in endless mode.

Jokers.effect: Each {{hl|orange|Queen}} held in hand gives {{mult|+13}}
Jokers.unlock: Play every Heart card in your deck in one round.
Jokers.syn:
===[[Decks]]===
*The {{D|Painted}} has a larger hand size, making this Joker easier to use.

===[[Poker hands]]===
All hands that do not use Queens benefit from this Joker.

In decks with a hand limit of 8 or less, hands that require 5 cards make this Joker more difficult to use. Conversely, smaller hands, such as High Card, can use this Joker effectively every hand.

This Joker may not be good when trying to make Straights, as the Straight cannot exceed a Jack unless {{J|Shortcut}} is in use.

===[[Jokers]]===
*{{J|Mime}} doubles the trigger of this Joker's effect.
*{{J|Midas Mask}} can add a buff to played Queens, providing an additional benefit thereafter when Queens are held in hand.
*{{J|Reserved Parking}} provides cash when face cards are held in hand.
*{{J|Baron}} increases the amount of Mult gained by {{xmult|1.5}} per held King, which can ride off of Shoot the Moon's Additive Mult for additional value. Shoot the Moon can also be used as a stepping stone for strengthening Queens to Kings for a Baron build.
**As previously mentioned, the player must physically move the Kings to the right of the Queens for maximum scoring value.
*{{J|Trading Card}} can remove non-Queen cards, allowing you to see and hold Queens easier.

===[[Consumables]]===
*{{Tarot|Death}} and {{Tarot|Strength}} can turn some cards into Queens.
*{{Tarot|The Hanged Man}} can remove non-Queen cards, allowing you to see and hold Queens easier.
*{{Tarot|The Chariot}} can turn some cards into Steel cards,
Jokers.anti:
===Decks===
*{{D|Abandoned}}, {{D|Mad World}}, and {{D|Medusa}} can be difficult to use, as they naturally contain no Queens.
*{{D|Five-Card Draw}} does not work well with this Joker due to the decreased hand size and banning of hand size-increasing Jokers.

===Jokers===
*Jokers that reduce hand size, like {{j|Stuntman}} and {{j|Merry Andy}}, will make the player hold fewer Queens.

===[[Blinds]]===
*{{Blind|The Hook}} discards 2 random cards after playing a hand, which may render Shoot the Moon useless if the Queens were discarded.
*{{Blind|The Plant}} debuffs all face cards, rendering Queens useless for the round.
*{{Blind|The Mark}} draws all face cards face down, which makes the player unable to tell which card is a Queen.
*{{Blind|Cerulean Bell}} may force a Queen to be played or discarded.
*{{Blind|Verdant Leaf}} debuffs all cards, including Queens, until a Joker is sold.
Jokers.strats:
If the player has any cards in hand that give {{xmult|1.5}}, either {{enhancement|Steel}}s or owning a {{J|Baron}}, it is ideal to manually drag the Queens to the far left so as to make Shoot the Moon's {{Hl|Red|+Mult}} trigger before the {{xMult|}}, maximizing the scoring power for the poker hand played. The reason for this is that any held-in-hand abilities are triggered from left to right. Therefore, placing any card far left will prioritize that specific held-in-hand effect. However, when enhancing a Queen itself to be a Steel card, the {{xMult|}} will always apply ''before'' Shoot the Moon's {{Hl|Red|+Mult}}.

The unlock requirement for Shoot the Moon does not necessarily mean to play one card of each rank with the Heart suit, so having just one Heart card in the deck and playing it will unlock Shoot the Moon. A suitable strategy to unlock it is with an {{D|Erratic}} configuration with few Hearts, or {{D|Abandoned}}, since it only has 10 Heart cards. Conversely, it is harder to unlock on {{D|Checkered}} due to the big amount of Heart cards.

Jokers.effect:
Allows {{ph|Straights}} to be made with gaps of {{hl|orange|1 rank}}
{{hl|gray|(ex: {{hl|orange|10 8 6 5 3}})}}
Jokers.syn:
===[[Decks]]===
*{{D|Black}}: The +1 Joker Slot allows Shortcut to function as a utility Joker while still providing space for 5 other Jokers to score.
*{{d|Abandoned}} lowers the range of card values from A-K to A-10, making it significantly more likely to draw a Straight, especially with Shortcut.
*{{D|Checkered}} in tandem with Shortcut increases the likelihood of finding a playable Straight Flush.
===[[Poker hands]]===
*{{ph|Straight}}
*{{ph|Straight Flush}} (or {{ph|Royal Flush}})
===[[Jokers]]===
*{{j|Four Fingers}} is a great combination with Shortcut, as this allows for a 4-length Straight with gaps, and Straight Flushes become even easier to make since the Straight and Flush don't need to be on the ''same'' 4 cards. (e.g. Q♠️ J♠️ 9♥️ 7♠️ 3♠️ is a valid Straight Flush with both Jokers in effect)
*{{j|Crazy Joker}} and {{j|The Order}} give additive and multiplicative Mult respectively when a Straight is played.
*{{j|Devious Joker}} and {{j|Runner}} both give Chips when a Straight is played.
*{{j|Superposition}} and {{j|Séance}} create [[Consumables]] when a Straight or Straight Flush is played.
*{{j|Space Joker}} and {{j|Burnt Joker}} appreciate Shortcut’s effect allowing for multiple straights to be formed in one round, and can make use of Straights having incredibly strong Planet scaling.
=== Playing cards ===
*Obtaining {{Planet|Saturn}} from cards with a {{Seal|Blue}} becomes much easier due to the decreased difficulty of forming a straight allowing more discards t
Jokers.strats: Mathematically, Shortcut is slightly better than {{j|Four Fingers}} in creating Straights.<ref>[https://www.reddit.com/r/balatro/comments/1b68mpp/statistical_analysis_of_the_four_fingers_and/ Statistical Analysis of the "Four Fingers" and "Shortcut" Jokers for Straights], a Reddit post</ref> However, Four Fingers is better at helping create Flushes and Straight Flushes. The player can consider choosing between the two, or combining the two to gain more Straights (in which case, Straights are almost always present in the 8 cards), but at the risk of losing two scoring Jokers.

Jokers.effect: [[Jokers|{{hl|orange|Joker}}]], {{Tarot|}}, {{Planet|}}, and {{Spectral|}} cards may appear multiple times
Jokers.unlock: Reach Ante level {{hl|orange|4}}
Jokers.syn:
===[[Decks]]===
Showman is effective with any deck, but is particularly strong on {{D|Black}} due to the +1 Joker slot bonus.

===[[Poker hands]]===
Showman has no direct effect on any specific poker hands. It does, however, make {{Booster|Celestial}}s less reliable, as its effect allows them to give duplicate planets. This decreases the chances of a Celestial Pack containing your desired Planet card, as well as preventing Planet Blocking (holding useless Planets in your consumable slots so they can't appear elsewhere) impossible.

===[[Jokers]]===
Showman has no direct Joker synergies. However, its main benefit lies in it being one of very few ways to obtain multiple copies of the same Joker.
*{{J|Cavendish}} is a powerful common Joker, making it likely to appear again before ante 8.
*{{J|Photograph}} and {{J|Hanging Chad}} have notable synergy and are also common Jokers, making them appear more often.
*{{J|Blueprint}} and {{J|Brainstorm}} are strong in long endless runs.
*{{J|The Idol}} is also powerful in endless runs.

===[[Vouchers]]===
Because it allows for duplicated Planet cards to appear, Showman synergizes with the {{V|Observatory}} by allowing for planet cards to appear in the shop whilst they are in the consumable space. However, this is easier achieved with {{Seal|Blue}}.

Showman can also create problems when {{V|Telescope}} is not yet redeemed, as {{Booster|Celestial}}s will often contain multiple copies of irrelevant planet cards.
Jokers.strats:
* Showman can make {{Tarot|The Emperor}} and {{J|Riff-Raff}} generate themselves.
* Although the probability is extremely low, Showman can even make multiple copies of {{Spectral|The Soul}} or {{Spectral|Black Hole}} appear in Booster Packs.
* If the player has Showman and finds a duplicate of any of their Jokers in the shop, if they sell that Joker and replace it with the shop duplicate, (as they might do if it has a better [[Edition]]) that Joker will be able to appear as a duplicate again even if the Showman is sold.

Jokers.effect:
If {{hl|orange|first hand}} of round is a single {{hl|orange|6}}, destroy it and create a {{Spectral|}} card
{{room}}
Jokers.syn:
===[[Decks]]===
*{{d|Red}} gives +1 Discard which makes it easier to find a 6.
*{{d|Blue}} gives +1 Hand which allows the player more freedom to utilize Sixth Sense, as there are more remaining Hands to defeat the Blind.
*{{d|Abandoned}} and {{D|Mad World}} increase the chance to draw a 6 as they have less overall cards.
*{{d|Painted}}  gives +2 hand size, making it easier to find 6s. However, the -1 joker slot makes Sixth Sense riskier to use.

*{{J|Drunkard}} and {{J|Merry Andy}} both give extra discards, which makes it easier to find a 6. While {{J|Merry Andy}} reduces hand size, which normally makes 6s harder to find, the extra discards will make that punishment pretty much meaningless, as long as the player does not reduce their hand size much lower.
*{{J|Juggler}} increases hand size and makes it easier to find a 6 to play. {{J|Troubadour}} and {{J|Turtle Bean}} can be used too, but Troubadour removes a hand, which makes it more punishing to use Sixth Sense, and Turtle Bean
Jokers.anti:
=== Decks ===
*{{D|Black}}, {{D|Blast Off}}, and {{D|Golden Needle}} all reduce the number of hands to play, which can discourage using Sixth Sense while a player's hands aren't strong enough.
*{{D|Nebula}} only starts with one Consumable Slot, which makes it harder to hold onto Sixth Sense's Spectral cards.

=== Jokers ===
*Obtaining a second copy of {{J|Sixth Sense}} does '''not''' stack with itself, creating only 1 Spectral card when destroying 6s.
*While {{J|Burglar}} gives more hands to play with, it also removes all discards. If the first hand of the round does not contain a 6, Sixth Sense will miss its effect.
*{{J|Stuntman}} reduces hand size, which makes it harder to find a 6.

=== [[Blinds]] ===
* {{Blind|The Psychic}} forces the player to play a 5-card hand, meaning Sixth Sense cannot activate.
* {{Blind|The Needle}} sets the player's hands to 1. Therefore, to still benefit fr
Jokers.strats:
As {{FULLPAGENAME}} requires having 6s in the deck to activate, it has limited use as the player will likely destroy all 6s in the Deck before reaching Ante 8. However, this is usually ideal, as 6s do not have any particularly strong synergies with other Jokers, and the Spectral card given may help further enhance the player's deck and hasten the Deck manipulation process. In general, Spectral cards to look out for are:
*Any of the Seal-adding cards.
** {{Spectral|Deja Vu}}, {{Spectral|Trance}}, {{Spectral|Medium}}, and {{Spectral|Talisman}}.
*{{Spectral|Aura}} for farming the {{edition|Polychrome}} Edition.
*{{Spectral|Cryptid}} to make copies of a useful card, which can be used in conjunction with the above Spectral cards.
*{{Spectral|Immolate}} to further hasten Deck manipulation and for a boost in Money.
*{{Spectral|Ectoplasm}} for when the player has their final Joker lineup.
Any other Spectral card is still worth keeping so as to prevent it from appearing in the shop, either from a {{Booster|Spectral}} or from playing on the {{D|Ghost}}, as they are either too niche or hard to make use of.

When using {{FULLPAGENAME}}, it can be worth opening {{Booster|Standard}}s to directly add 6s for later destruction; while this usually isn't as good as opening a Spectral Pack directly, Standard Packs are much more common than Spectral Packs, and Spectral cards can be quite impactful. Additionally, {{FULLPAGENAME}} makes it more reasonable to fish for specific or highly-upgraded car

Jokers.effect: {{Chips|+50}} if played hand contains a {{ph|Pair}}
Jokers.syn:
===[[Decks]]===
*The {{D|Abandoned}} and {{D|Mad World}}, having fewer total cards in the deck, gives a higher chance of drawing a pair.
*The {{D|Erratic}} will have cards of a certain rank appear more than others.

Spare Trousers's additive Mult increases by +2 any time the player plays a Poker Hand that contains a {{Ph|Two Pair}}. A {{Ph|Two Pair}}, a {{Ph|Full House}}, or a {{Ph|Flush House}} will always trigger this increase, even if any of the cards are debuffed by a [[Blinds and Antes|Boss Blind]]. A {{Ph|Flush}} may also trigger this increase if it is assembled in such a way that it also contains a Two Pair; for example, a valid {{Ph|Flush}} for Spare Trousers would be K K J 9 9 with a matching suit.

===[[Jokers]]===
*{{J|Square Joker}}: {{Chips|+4}} any time a played hand consists of exactly four cards. Since a standard Two Pair is exactly four cards, the player can strengthen both Square Joker and Spare Trousers at the same time.
*{{J|Space Joker}}: Like with Supernova, the repeated playing of Two Pair synergizes well with this Joker.
*{{J|Card Sharp}}: Because it's unlikely to win with one Two Pair hand, Card Sharp will provide an additional {{xmult|3}} on subsequent Two Pair hands.

Jokers.anti:
===Decks===
*{{D|Black}}, {{D|Blast Off}}, and {{D|Golden Needle}} all have poor synergy with Spare Trousers due to their reduced number of hands.
===Poker hands===
*[[5 of a kind]], [[Four of a Kind]], [[Three of a Kind]], [[Pair]], [[Straight]], [[Royal Flush]], and [[Flush Five]] cannot activate the +Mult ability.
===[[Blinds]]===
*{{Blind|The Eye}} will only allow the player to play any given Poker Hand once, limiting the scaling opportunities for Spare Trousers.
Jokers.strats: Spare Trousers' usefulness is comparable to a bell curve over time. Initially, Spare Trousers has no bonus, and the player needs to play a Two Pair hand for it to have any benefit at all. Since any played hand can only ever include one Two Pair at a time, it can potentially take numerous hands and rounds of a run to build up Spare Trousers to a point where it feels strong. In other words, Spare Trousers requires a significant time investment, plus a conscious effort to play as many Two Pair hands as possible. Furthermore, since it can only be increased by +2 Mult per hand at most, in the late game (beginning around Ante level 7 and higher) the player runs the risk of being unable to increase Spare Trousers quickly enough to keep it viable. Usually, the player can raise Spare Trousers to around +40 Mult by the time they reach Ante level 8, but if Spare Trousers was the centerpiece of their build, they may struggle against the Showdown Blind and any subsequent Boss Blinds. Using [[Planet cards]] to level up Spare Trousers' applicable hands can partially compensate for the joker's late-game strength falloff.

===[[Poker hands]]===

*{{ph|Straight Flush}} (and {{ph|Royal Flush}}) with an Ace.
===[[Jokers]]===
*{{j|Shortcut}}: Normally, there are only two possible straights that contain an ace: A/2/3/4/5 and 10/J/Q/K/A. This makes it relatively difficult to trigger Superposition. Shortcut, however, allows straights to skip single cards, vastly increasing the number of ways this joker can be triggered.

===[[Decks]]===
*{{D|Blue}} works best with Troubadour thanks to its +1 hand per round bonus, offsetting the -1 hand penalty of this Joker. This effectively transforms the Blue Deck into a more flexible {{d|Painted}}.
*{{D|Golden Needle}} starts with 1 hand, and Troubadour cannot reduce hands below one, turning Troubadour into a +2 hand size without any penalty.

===[[Poker Hands]]===
Any strong 5 card hands can benefit from Troubadour, as the increased hand size means a higher chance to draw needed cards to form the hand.

Troubadour can also be good in High-card builds that rely on cards being in hand to score, such as with {{J|Baron}} or Steel cards.
===[[Jokers]]===
*Any held-in-hand effect Joker will be improved by Troubadour by virtue of holding more cards in hand.
** This includes {{J|Baron}}, as mentioned previously, {{J|Shoot the Moon}}, and {{J|Reserved Parking}}.
*{{J|Mime}}: More cards in hand means more cards for Mime to retrigger.
*{{J|Mail-In Rebate}}: With increased hand size, it can be easier to find the card rank required for that round.
*{{J|Burglar}}: Add three extra hands, offsetting the -1 hand penalty of this Joker at the cost of no discards.
*{{J|Merry Andy}} and {{J|Stuntman}}: Troubadour offsets the hand size penalty of these two Jokers.

===[[Card modifiers]]===
With Troubadour's increased hand size, it can make it easier to draw into {{enhancement|Steel}}s and/or {{enhancement|Gold}}s, as well as cards that have a {{Seal|Blue}}.

===[[Vouchers]]===
Jokers.anti:

*{{j|Loyalty Card}} becomes harder

===Jokers===
*Jokers that rely on specific card enhancements become harder to use when combined with Vampire. These include {{J|Lucky Cat}}, {{J|Glass Joker}}, {{J|Golden Ticket}}, {{J|Steel Joker}} and {{J|Stone Joker}}.
*{{J|Driver's License}} limits the players to not play any enhanced card, making a risky combo with Vampire.

===Vouchers===
*{{V|Planet Merchant}} and {{V|Planet Tycoon}} reduce the probabilities of Tarot cards appearing in the shop, and therefore, the {{xmult|}} from Vampire. {{V|Magic Trick}} also applies here, but this one isn't too bad at all since it's required to get {{V|Illusion}}.
Jokers.strats:
Vampire removes Enhancements before their effect occurs, meaning the Enhancements cannot activate. All scored cards will get their Enhancements removed. Vampire also cannot change the type of [[Poker Hands|Poker Hand]] retroactively, for example removing {{Enhancement|Wild|name=Wild}} would still keep the Poker Hand as {{ph|Flush}}.

There are a few notable playing card interactions:
* [[Debuffed]]: Debuffed cards are considered not to have any Modifier including Enhancements, so Vampire cannot remove Enhancements from debuffed cards.
* {{Enhancement|Wild}}: wild enhancement gets removed, the card scores if it would have scored for the original hand, and the type of hand played is not affected.
* {{Enhancement|Glass}}: glass enhancement gets removed, no {{xmult|2}}, and there is no chance for the card to break.
* {{Enhancement|Stone}}: stone enhancement gets removed and card returns to what it originally was, no {{chips|+50}}, but card will always score for this hand (the type of hand played is not affected).
* [[Editions]]: Editions are not Enhancements, will not get removed by Vampire, and work normally.
* [[Seals]]: Seals are not Enhancements, will not get removed by Vampire, and work normally.
The Joker order matters significantly when using certain other Jokers with Vampire:
* A second {{J|Vampire}}: only the left-most Vampire can remove enhancements and scale at any time (regardless of how many Midas Masks are used).
* {{J|Midas Mask}}:
** Putting Midas Mask before Vamp

Wee Joker synergizes well with all Decks fairly equally, but some have minor advantages over the others.

Most decks have the same starting amount of four 2s, making Wee Joker synergize with them fairly equally. However, some decks have features that may make utilizing Wee Joker easier:
* {{d|Red}}: The extra {{hl|red|Discard}} allows the player to cycle through more cards, which helps with finding and scoring 2s greatly.
* {{d|Blue}}: The extra {{hl|blue|Hand}} lets the player use a "throwaway" hand for extra scaling, and also acts as a pseudo-Discard, again helping with finding and scoring 2s.

Try copying a {{Tarot|Death}} to convert cards into 2s, or {{Tarot|The Hanged Man}} to get rid of many non-2s at once.
* {{d|Ghost}}: Thanks to its easier access to [[Spectral cards]], the Ghost Deck has great potential to manipulate the deck into being beneficial to Wee Joker. Try looking for {{Spectral|Cryptid}} to create multiple new 2s, or {{Spectral|Deja Vu}} to put a red seal on an existing 2.
* {{d|Abandoned}} and {{D|Mad World}}: Due to the small size of the deck, the likelihood of stumbling across 2s on these deck is very much better, and thus allows for more efficient scaling.
* {{d|Painted}

* Cryptid creates 2 copies of 1 selected card in the player's hand. This effect is very powerful for helping the player find a specific card wanted, as it is basically tripling a specific card in the deck with pretty much no downside with just one use.
* Cryptid can be used to copy cards that already have a good Enhancement, Edition and/or Seal. ex: {{Seal|Red|image=Glass Card.png}} [[Glass card|Glass]] {{Edition|Polychrome|type=Playing Card}} {{F|King}}.
* Using Cryptid is highly beneficial to most builds, ranging from {{ph|High Card}} to {{ph|Flush Five}} builds. Inversely, it may not work very well for {{ph|Straight}}/{{ph|Straight Flush}} builds, as the sudden influx of a rank may make it harder to find other ranks.
* Cryptid bypasses the hand size limit, which can be useful in a {{ph|High Card}} build utilizing {{Enhancement|Steel}}s if the player has a way to hold multiple copies o

Spectral Cards.st:
* Ectoplasm grants a random Joker the {{Edition|Negative}} making it give +1 [[Joker slot]] and essentially frees up a Joker slot. This amazing effect is held back greatly by its -1 extra Hand size for each Ectoplasm used throughout the run, which can be a run killer if not used carefully, especially when considering how valuable Hand sizes are.
* Ectoplasm is oftentimes used to help the run for longer. By having more Joker slots, the player can potentially find new Jokers that can help the run out significantly, or duplicates of strong Jokers already owned when paired with {{J|Showman}}.
* Ectoplasm can only target Jokers with the {{Edition|Base}} Edition, which means it is possible to force the hand of fate and make it hit the Joker that is wanted easily.

Spectral Cards.st:
* Hex acts as a one-time use  {{Tarot|The Wheel of Fortune}} that always gives Polychrome, with downsides attached. Hex becomes significantly stronger From {{Stake|Black}} onwards due to the presence of Eternal Jokers, which cannot be destroyed.
* Hex destroys Jokers, which means it is sometimes a good idea to sell all Jokers that you don't wish to be Polychrome, or that you can survive without.
** If all Eternal Jokers have editions and you have a non-Eternal Joker that has no edition, then Hex is guaranteed to hit the non-Eternal Joker.

Spectral Cards.st:
* Ouija converts all cards held in hand into a random rank at the cost of 1 Hand size afterwards. This effect, while essentially being a huge gamble on most occasions, can be of great benefit if used properly and will help tremendously when used early enough, often giving a clear direction for deck-fixing later into the run.
* While being amazing when used early, Ouija falls off surprisingly quickly if it's found too late into the run. Most builds aim towards a few specific ranks to work, and Ouija having a (fixed) 1/13 chance for the desired rank can mess that up if not used with caution.
* The -1 Hand size given from using Ouija can be detrimental in a lot of cases, and as such, it is advised not to use Ouija when combined with other Hand size deduction effects such as {{J|Stuntman}} or {{Spectral|Ectoplasm}}.

Spectral Cards.st:
* The Soul creates a random [[Legendary Joker]] if the player has room. This is one of the rarest cards in Balatro, only having a 0.3% chance to replace a card, for every card in the pack, in Arcana Packs and Spectral Packs. It is typically very powerful, and can be the sole reason the player wins a run if used properly.
* One way to find The Soul is to repeatedly reset and skip for the {{Tag|Charm}}, which has a small chance to contain The Soul.
** An {{Tag|Ethereal}} will not work as well as the Charm Tag, since the [[Spectral Pack]] given has only 2 cards compared to [[Mega Arcana Pack]]'s 5 cards, and as the chance is rolled independently for each card in the pack, it has a higher chance of giving The Soul. In addition, Charm Tags can be found on Ante 1, whereas Ethereal Tags can only be found on Ante 2+.
* The Soul cannot generate {{Sticker|Eternal}} Jokers, which might hinder its p

Spectral Cards.st:
* Wraith creates a random Rare Joker if there is room and sets money to {{$|0}}. This effect can potentially be life-saving due to how strong Rare Jokers can be, but may give little benefits if the Joker it generates doesn't fit into the run.
* Wraith can be used to remove debt completely, which can work surprisingly well to remove the downsides of using {{J|Credit Card}} or {{blind|The Tooth}} boss blind.
* If the build is already good enough on its own, it may not be wise to give up a Joker and use Wraith, because the Joker it generates may not be beneficial to the run and in turn can be run-killing.
* It is a good idea to spend down before using Wraith, which will help minimize its downside and allow you to see more shop items.

Vouchers.st: As mentioned above, [[Spectral cards]] are most useful for their deck fixing potential. With powerful spectral cards such as {{Spectral|Deja Vu}} and {{Spectral|Immolate}} able to alter or destroy cards in a more significant ways than tarot cards. It is generally recommended to pair with as many other sources of spectral or tarot cards to maximise this effect to draw powerful cards as consistently as possible. Also, it is generally better to receive Omen Globe early into the run, giving the most time to deck fix and to gain value out of {{Spectral|Hex}} and {{Spectral|Ankh}} before having multiple powerful jokers.

Tags.st:
*As the {{Edition|Foil}} Edition is the most commonly obtainable Edition, either by natural means, purchasing {{V|Hone}} and {{V|Glow Up}}, or successfully activating a {{Tarot|The Wheel of Fortune}}, this Tag may seem underwhelming at first. However, having a single Foil Edition Joker can supplement or remove the need to obtain a Chips dedicated Joker.
*This Tag is also significantly more beneficial on the {{D|Plasma}} which benefits more in the early to mid game from Chips value, making it a potentially worthwhile skip in an early Ante.

Tags.st: * The Investment Tag is considered by many players to be one of the best, if not the best tag in the game, especially if found early on. Unless the player is in massive debt, {{money|25}} is usually enough money to buy plenty of things at [[the Shop]], as well as instantly hitting the [[interest]] cap (assuming the player doesn't have the {{J|Seed Money}} voucher). As players progress during the run and get their economy under control, the Investment Tag becomes less worth it unless the player is really in a pinch, especially since the tag only takes effect once beating the Boss Blind and the player can potentially make more than {{money|25}} just by playing through the Antes normally depending on their build. During {{Stake|Purple}} and higher, the scores necessary to progress further in the Antes becomes too high to afford skipping at least one Shop over.

Enhancements.st: Stone cards are best utilized when playing low scoring poker hands, like {{Ph|High Card}} or {{Ph|Pair}}. They can supplement your Chips while your Jokers and hand levels provide {{Mult|}}. They fall off in scoring potential towards the late game, so they're best used while you look for more {{Planet|}} cards and scoring Jokers. If playing on the {{D|Plasma}}, Stone cards have a lot more late game potential. While they will eventually be outpaced by Blind scaling, they can easily win you a run with the right setup.

Seals.st:
* It is recommended to put Gold Seals on cards intended to be played often, and cards that can naturally be retriggered by certain Jokers, like face cards for {{J|Sock and Buskin}} or 2s, 3s, 4s, 5s for {{J|Hack}}.
* It is always a good idea to play a Gold Seal card, even if it doesn't contribute much to the score, if the player has spare hands. Losing {{money|1}} for playing a hand and gaining at least {{money|3}} back is almost always a good trade-off.

<section begin="medium_usage" /><!-- These content transclusion to Medium -->
*Counterintuitively, Purple Seals should be put on high value cards. This is because although they incentivize those cards to be discarded, they also incentivize those cards to be duplicated. When many of the duplicated cards are in the deck, they provide far greater value.
*Purple Seal cards should also be duplicated with {{Tarot|Death}} with higher priority than other cards, even if the other cards are more powerful. This is because the new Purple Seal cards can be used to generate more {{Tarot|Death}} cards, exponentially increasing the number of Purple Seals and allowing the more powerful cards to be quickly and easily duplicated later in the run.
*Purple Seals are most powerful to obtain early game, as obtaining one later does not allow it to be duplicated as much, and it will provide far less value.
